Statement 5 mischaracterizes universal quantifiers as things that "must be strictly avoided," when the syllabus actually places them in the "use with care" category, not the "avoid" category — so statement 5 is False.

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's new VP of Operations argues that formal Requirements Engineering is unnecessary for the QuickBag rollout because "everyone already knows what a bag-drop kiosk should do." Which of the following is **NOT** one of the benefits that adequate RE adds to a project, according to the syllabus?

options.text: Enabling a better understanding of the problem
Providing a basis for estimating development effort and cost
Reducing the risk of developing the wrong system
Providing a prerequisite for testing the system
Guaranteeing that the delivered system will have zero defects

questions.explanation: The syllabus lists reducing the risk of developing the wrong system, better problem understanding, a basis for cost/effort estimation, and a prerequisite for testing as RE benefits — it never claims RE guarantees zero defects, which is an overclaim.

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's hardware integration team writes: "WHEN the conveyor belt scale detects a bag weighing more than 32 kg, the kiosk shall display an excess-weight message and shall not print a bag tag." Using the EARS phrase templates, this requirement is best classified as:
questions.explanation: The sentence follows the EARS structure "WHEN `<trigger>` the `<system>` shall `<response>`," which is the event-driven template, regardless of the fact that the triggering condition describes an exceptional situation. The unwanted-behavior template specifically uses "IF ... THEN," not "WHEN."

questions.prompt: During elicitation, almost no passenger mentions wanting the kiosk to correctly print a legible bag tag — everyone simply assumes it will work, but complaints would be severe if tags frequently printed unreadable. Meanwhile, a few passengers express delight at an unexpected feature letting them pre-select a seat upgrade directly at the kiosk. According to the Kano model, these two requirements are respectively classified as:
questions.explanation: A requirement nobody mentions but that causes severe dissatisfaction if unmet is a dissatisfier (basic factor); an unexpected feature that delights a few passengers is a delighter (excitement factor), per the Kano model.

questions.prompt: A SkyHarbor product owner writes the following backlog item: "As a passenger, I want a self-service bag-drop kiosk." Using Cohn's classic user-story phrase template ("As a `<role>`, I want `<requirement>`, so that `<benefit>`"), what is the main structural problem with this user story?

options.text: It violates a rule that user stories must be modeled in UML
It omits the benefit clause, so the underlying need/value is not expressed
It is written as a use case instead of a user story
It fails to name a stakeholder role at all

questions.explanation: The user story names a role ("passenger") and a requirement ("a self-service bag-drop kiosk") but omits the "so that `<benefit>`" clause, so the underlying value/need is not expressed.
questions.reference: EU3.3 — Phrase Templates for User Stories

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's IT department introduces a tool that stores each QuickBag requirement's attributes, lets the team prioritize backlog items, manages versions and baselines, and tracks forward/backward traceability to test cases. Per the syllabus's categories of RE tool support, this tool primarily supports:
questions.explanation: Storing attributes, prioritizing, managing versions/configurations, and tracking/tracing requirements are explicitly grouped under "management of requirements" tooling in the syllabus, distinct from RE-process management, modeling, or documentation-of-knowledge tooling.

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's RE team drafts a use case named "Self-Tag a Bag" describing how a passenger tags their own bag at the QuickBag kiosk. For each of the following, judge whether it is information a use case form template would typically be expected to include (Applicable) or not (Not applicable).

statements.text: The primary actor (e.g., "Passenger")
A main success scenario describing the normal step-by-step flow
The exact UML class diagram for the kiosk's internal software architecture
Preconditions that must hold before the use case can start (e.g., passenger has checked in)
Alternative/exception flows (e.g., bag exceeds weight limit)

questions.explanation: Use case form templates (per Cockburn, as referenced in the syllabus) typically capture actors, preconditions, the main success scenario, and extensions/alternative flows — but not a UML class diagram of internal software architecture, which belongs to a structure/data model, not a use case.
questions.reference: EU3.3 — Form Templates for Use Cases

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's RE team (a) silently observes ground-handling agents at the current manual check-in counters for two full shifts without interrupting them, and (b) reviews the existing legacy check-in system's user manual and incident logs to understand current pain points. Name the two categories of gathering techniques that activities (a) and (b) respectively represent.
questions.explanation: Silent, unobtrusive observation of agents is an observation technique; reviewing manuals and logs is an artifact-based technique. Neither is a questioning technique (which involves direct dialogue) nor a collaboration technique (which involves joint activities with stakeholders).

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's documentation lead decides to introduce form templates for all QuickBag use cases and phrase templates for individual requirements, replacing free-form prose. Name the two genuine advantages of template-based work products described in the syllabus that this change can be expected to deliver.

options.text: It guarantees that every requirement author will focus on content rather than merely filling in fields
It helps capture the most relevant information consistently
It provides a clear, reusable structure across all requirements
It automatically resolves all stakeholder conflicts about requirement content
It eliminates the need for any natural-language text within requirements

questions.explanation: Templates provide a clear, reusable structure and help capture the most relevant information — both explicitly listed advantages. They do not guarantee content focus (that is listed as a pitfall/risk), do not eliminate natural language, and do not resolve stakeholder conflicts.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is **NOT** an example of explicit traceability, as described in the syllabus, for the QuickBag requirements?

options.text: A traceability matrix stored in a spreadsheet linking requirements to test cases
Wiki-style hyperlinks in the specification connecting a requirement to its related model element
A dedicated "Source" attribute on each requirement, pointing to the stakeholder interview it originated from
Everyone on the team simply remembering, through consistent naming conventions, that requirements starting with "SEC-" always come from the security screening regulations

questions.explanation: Relying on informal, memorized naming conventions is an example of *implicit* traceability (achieved through structuring/standardizing work products), not explicit traceability, which requires documented relationships based on unique identifiers (attributes, matrices, hyperlinks, graphs).

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's draft context diagram for QuickBag shows the system interacting with: Passenger, Ground-Handling Staff, and the Airline Departure Control System. Given that every self-tagged bag must also be electronically cleared against a watch-list before it is accepted onto the conveyor, which actor is most clearly missing from this context model?

options.text: The kiosk's internal receipt printer driver
The Border Protection Unit's security/customs screening system

questions.explanation: Since bags must be cleared against a watch-list before conveyor acceptance, the security/customs screening system is a context actor that interacts with QuickBag and is missing from the diagram. The other options are not RE-relevant context actors in the sense of a context model.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is **NOT** listed in the syllabus as an example of a design and idea-generating technique for requirements elicitation?
questions.explanation: Brainstorming, analogies, scenarios, and storyboards are explicitly named design and idea-generating techniques. Structured one-to-one interviews are a questioning (gathering) technique, used to elicit mostly conscious, already-known requirements.

questions.prompt: In a UML class diagram for QuickBag's domain model, a single "Booking" may be associated with several "Bag" instances, but each "Bag" belongs to exactly one "Booking." Which UML class diagram element correctly expresses this requirement?

options.text: A state transition from Booking to Bag
An association between the Booking and Bag classes, with multiplicity 1 on the Booking end and 0..* (or 1..*) on the Bag end
A generalization relationship where Bag inherits from Booking
An activity edge connecting a Booking action to a Bag action

questions.explanation: A "1-to-many" ownership relationship (one Booking, many Bags, each Bag tied to exactly one Booking) is expressed as an association with multiplicity 1 on the Booking side and 0..*/1..* on the Bag side in a UML class diagram — not generalization, which would imply an is-a relationship, nor activity/state elements, which are not structural.

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's RE team captures the following two statements during early scoping of QuickBag: (1) "The airport wants to reduce average bag-drop time to under 90 seconds to increase gate turnaround revenue." (2) "Ground-handling agents want a kiosk override button so they can manually confirm an oversized bag." Name the two requirement occurrence types that statements (1) and (2) respectively represent.
questions.explanation: Statement (1) expresses a business goal (increasing revenue through faster turnaround) — a business requirement. Statement (2) expresses what ground-handling agents, as users of the kiosk's staff-facing functions, want from their own perspective — a user requirement.

questions.prompt: Judge whether each of the following statements about modeling the QuickBag bag-drop process with a UML activity diagram is TRUE or FALSE, per the CPRE Foundation Level syllabus.

statements.text: An activity diagram can model the sequence of actions from "Scan Boarding Pass" to "Print Bag Tag" to "Release onto Conveyor."
An activity diagram can express decision points, such as branching into an "Overweight" path versus a "Within Limit" path.
An activity diagram can show which actor/role (e.g., passenger vs. ground staff) is responsible for a given action.
At the CPRE Foundation Level, activity diagrams are expected to model detailed data-flow between actions using advanced modeling elements.
Activity diagrams are only usable for business processes and can never be used to specify a system function.

questions.explanation: Activity diagrams model action sequences (1), decision/branch points (2), and can show responsibility for actions (3) — all explicitly supported. Detailed data-flow modeling requires advanced elements not covered at Foundation Level (4 is false), and activity diagrams are explicitly usable for specifying system functions, not only business processes (5 is false).

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's RE team encounters several disagreements while specifying QuickBag. For each situation below, judge whether it is correctly classified as the stated conflict type.

statements.text: FlyNova Airlines' operations team and the Border Protection Unit genuinely need different things from the bag-drop deadline — ops wants it open until 20 minutes before departure, security needs 45 minutes for screening — due to the different nature of their respective tasks. This is a **subject matter conflict**.

The ground-handling contract states the maximum bag weight is 32 kg, while the airline's own fare-rules document states 30 kg, and nobody has reconciled the two documents. This is a **data conflict**.

One stakeholder refuses to cooperate with another because of a dispute from an unrelated past project, long before QuickBag existed, and emotions are running high. This is best described as a **structural conflict**.

Two managers disagree because one reports to IT and the other reports to Ground Operations, and the two departments compete for the same limited budget allocated to QuickBag. This is a **structural conflict**.
A conflict based purely on differing personal principles and values between two stakeholders about how much automation is acceptable is an **interest conflict**.

questions.explanation: Differing factual task needs between ops and security is a subject matter conflict (1, true); inconsistent documents about bag weight is a data conflict (2, true). The past-dispute/emotional scenario (3) is a relationship conflict, not structural, so it is false; competing departments over limited budget and reporting lines (4) is indeed structural, so true. Differing personal principles about automation (5) is a value conflict, not an interest conflict, so false.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about process models and activity models in RE is **INCORRECT**?

options.text: BPMN is a modeling language that was standardized specifically and exclusively for modeling class structures, not processes
Process models can be used to describe either business processes or technical processes
At the CPRE Foundation Level, only UML activity diagrams are used for process modeling, even though other languages such as BPMN also exist
Activity models are primarily used to specify system functions

questions.explanation: BPMN is a process modeling language (an alternative to UML activity diagrams for business/technical processes), not a language for modeling class structures — making A the incorrect statement. B, C, and D accurately reflect the syllabus.

questions.prompt: Three SkyHarbor stakeholder groups cannot agree on a single bag-drop deadline policy. Management decides to simply let the airline's Head of Ground Operations make the final binding call without further negotiation. Which conflict resolution technique is being applied?
questions.explanation: Letting one party make the final binding decision for everyone else, without further negotiation, is the definition of overruling — distinct from agreement, compromise, voting (involving multiple parties' votes), or defining separate variants.

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's RE team needs to specify how the QuickBag kiosk reacts differently to a boarding-pass scan depending on whether it is currently in state Idle, Scanning, or OutOfService, including the transitions and actions triggered by each event. Which model type is best suited for this purpose?
questions.explanation: Specifying state-dependent reactions to events, including transitions and triggered actions, is exactly what a state machine/statechart is used for. A context diagram, class model, and goal model do not capture this dynamic, state-dependent behavior.

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's QA lead argues that requirements validation is complete once the RE team itself re-reads the QuickBag specification one single time. Name two important aspects for requirements validation that this approach is missing.

options.text: Involvement of the right stakeholders (not just the RE team itself)
Repeated validation rather than a single pass
Separating the identification of defects from their correction

questions.explanation: A single self-review by the RE team misses involvement of the right stakeholders (who were not consulted) and repeated validation (only one pass was done). The scenario does not clearly indicate a problem with separating defect identification from correction.

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's RE team wants to (1) visualize the conflicting goal of "minimize passenger wait time" versus "maximize security screening thoroughness" together with the obstacles standing in the way, and separately wants to (2) create a visual, domain-specific-symbol story of how a ground agent, a bag, and the conveyor physically interact during an oversized-bag exception. Name the two model types that respectively fit situations (1) and (2).
questions.explanation: Representing competing goals and the obstacles between them is exactly what a goal model is for; visually depicting how actors, bags, and devices interact using domain-specific symbols is the purpose of a domain story model. Interaction models (sequence diagrams), block definition diagrams, and context diagrams serve different purposes.
questions.reference: EU3.4.6 — Further Model Types in RE

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor wants to compare two slightly different kiosk check-in flows by rolling each one out to a different subset of real passengers over two weeks and measuring which flow produces shorter average bag-drop times. Which requirements validation technique does this best describe?
questions.explanation: Rolling out two variants to different passenger subsets and comparing a measured outcome is the defining characteristic of A/B testing, an exploratory validation technique — distinct from reviews (walkthroughs/inspections) and from building a single MVP.

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's reviewer is assessing the QuickBag system requirements specification against the syllabus's quality criteria. Judge each statement as TRUE or FALSE.

statements.text: A requirement stating "The kiosk shall be fast" fails the "unambiguous" and "verifiable" criteria for single requirements, since "fast" is not objectively measurable.
"Adequate" and "understandable" are described as the most important quality criteria for a single requirement, since without them a requirement is useless even if all other criteria are met.

Two requirements in the specification that contradict each other about the maximum bag weight (32 kg in one section, 30 kg in another) violate the "consistent" quality criterion for work products covering multiple requirements.
"Traceable" is listed as a quality criterion for a single requirement in isolation, not for work products covering multiple requirements.
A specification is "conformant" when it adheres to applicable templates, standards, or regulations imposed on the document.

questions.explanation: "Fast" is vague and not measurable, failing unambiguous/verifiable (1, true). Adequate and understandable are indeed named as the most important criteria for single requirements (2, true). Contradictory weight limits violate consistency across the work product (3, true). Traceable is listed as a quality criterion for work products covering *multiple* requirements, not for an isolated single requirement, so statement 4 is false. Conformance to templates/standards/regulations is exactly what "conformant" means (5, true).
questions.reference: EU3.8 — Quality Criteria for Work Products and Requirements

questions.prompt: Judge whether each of the following statements about the need for requirements validation is TRUE or FALSE.

statements.text: Validation of requirements can be safely deferred entirely until the system has been deployed, since only real usage can reveal whether stakeholders are satisfied.
One purpose of validation is to check whether agreement about the requirements has been achieved among the stakeholders.
Validation should also check whether the context assumptions underlying the requirements are reasonable.
Validating a requirements document once, early in the project, makes any later re-validation unnecessary.

questions.explanation: Validation must start already during RE, not be deferred entirely to post-deployment (1, false). Checking stakeholder agreement (2) and the reasonableness of context assumptions (3) are both explicitly named validation checks (true). Validation should be repeated, not performed only once (4, false).

questions.prompt: Before committing to the final touchscreen layout, SkyHarbor's UX designer builds a clickable screen-by-screen simulation of the kiosk's boarding flow using design software — passengers can tap through screens exactly as they would on the real kiosk, but no backend logic actually processes bags or prints tags. Which kind of prototype is this?
questions.explanation: A click-through simulation using real screens but no real backend functionality is, by definition, a mock-up (medium-fidelity exploratory prototype) — as opposed to a low-fidelity wireframe, a high-fidelity native prototype with working functionality, or an evolutionary prototype that forms the core of the final system.

questions.prompt: TagTech Systems, the kiosk vendor, proposes to SkyHarbor's management: "Just buy our biometric facial-recognition boarding module — it's state of the art and will modernize your airport." No analysis of the actual bag-drop/boarding problem or passenger needs has been performed yet. Which RE principle is most directly being violated?

options.text: Principle 8 (Innovation) — the proposal lacks sufficient innovation
Principle 5 (Problem – Requirement – Solution) — a solution is being adopted before the underlying problem and requirements have been clarified
Principle 9 (Systematic and disciplined work) — no RE process has been tailored yet
Principle 2 (Stakeholders) — not all stakeholders have been consulted

questions.explanation: Adopting a specific solution (a biometric module) before the underlying problem and requirements have been analyzed directly violates Principle 5 (Problem – Requirement – Solution), which stresses that a solution should emerge from understood problems and requirements, not precede them. D is a plausible but weaker distractor, since the issue here is specifically a solution-before-problem jump, not merely "no process."

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's National Civil Aviation Authority requires a comprehensive, formally released QuickBag requirements specification before any development may legally begin, and the delivered system will be outsourced to an external contractor under a fixed-scope contract. Which RE process time-facet configuration best fits this situation?

options.text: Neither linear nor iterative applies to regulated systems
Iterative, because regulatory review always requires multiple short feedback loops
Linear, because a comprehensive specification is required as a contractual/regulatory basis before development starts
Iterative, because the contractor will need to adapt the requirements as development proceeds

questions.explanation: A regulator requiring a comprehensive, formally released specification before development begins, combined with outsourcing to an external contractor under a fixed contract, are textbook criteria for choosing a linear RE process, as listed in the syllabus.
questions.reference: EU5.2 — Requirements Engineering Process Facets (Time Facet)

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's RE team releases "QuickBag Requirements Baseline v1.0" ahead of the pilot kiosk rollout. Name two of the properties the syllabus attributes to such a configuration/baseline.

options.text: Redundancy — it is expected to duplicate content found elsewhere for convenience
Consistency — the set of work products it contains is internally consistent
Unchangeability — once established, the baseline can serve as a fixed reference point
Ambiguity — some latitude for differing interpretation is acceptable in a baseline
Flexibility — any team member may silently edit the baseline at any time without recording the change

questions.explanation: The syllabus lists unchangeability and consistency (along with logical connection, uniqueness, and basis for reset) as properties of configurations/baselines. A baseline is change-controlled, not freely editable (ruling out B), and is not expected to be redundant or ambiguous.

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor cannot interview every possible passenger who will use the QuickBag kiosks, since the traveling public is anonymous and constantly changing. To still represent this stakeholder group adequately during elicitation, the RE team should:

options.text: Interview only frequent flyers, since they are the most experienced stakeholders
Define a small set of fictional, archetypical passenger personas representing the relevant end-user groups
Postpone passenger-related requirements until after the kiosks are deployed and feedback arrives
Skip passenger requirements entirely and rely only on ground staff and airline ops input

questions.explanation: When individual end users cannot be identified or interviewed, the syllabus recommends defining personas as fictional archetypical substitutes representing relevant end-user groups, rather than skipping, over-narrowing, or deferring passenger requirements.

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor later launches a second, purely internal pilot to let ground staff experiment with an evolving set of QuickBag kiosk features over several months, with frequent feedback sessions and no fixed external contract. Name two criteria from the syllabus that would justify choosing an iterative RE process for this pilot.

options.text: Many requirements are not known up front but will emerge and evolve during development
A comprehensive requirements specification is required as a contractual basis for outsourcing
Stakeholders are available such that short feedback loops can be established
The development process for the system is plan-driven and mostly linear
Regulatory authorities require a formally released specification at an early stage

questions.explanation: Requirements emerging/evolving during development and availability of stakeholders for short feedback loops are both explicit criteria for choosing an iterative RE process. B, D, and E are criteria favoring a linear process instead.
questions.reference: EU5.2 — Requirements Engineering Process Facets (Time Facet)

questions.prompt: Judge whether each of the following statements about requirements life cycle management, versioning, and change handling at SkyHarbor is TRUE or FALSE.

statements.text: A life cycle model is needed to define which status transitions (e.g., draft to reviewed to agreed) are allowed for a QuickBag requirement.
Once a work product has any version history, keeping track of what specifically changed between versions is unnecessary as long as a version number exists.
In a linear, plan-driven part of the QuickBag project, a Change Control Board is a typical mechanism for deciding on proposed requirement changes.
In the more iterative pilot, it would be consistent with agile practice for the product owner to add a requested change as a new backlog item and prioritize it accordingly.
Requirements are static once documented, so version control is only relevant for source code, not for requirements work products.

questions.explanation: A life cycle model defining allowed statuses/transitions is required (1, true). Version control requires tracking *what* changed, not just a version number (2, false). A Change Control Board is the typical linear/plan-driven change mechanism (3, true); in agile contexts the product owner manages change via the backlog (4, true). Requirements are explicitly described as subject to evolution, so version control applies to requirements work products too (5, false).
questions.reference: EU6.3/6.7 — Version Control and Handling Change

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's QuickBag project involves a domestic in-house IT team and an outsourced UI design agency located overseas, with high staff turnover on the agency side. Name the three factors from the syllabus that are explicitly identified as obstacles to achieving shared understanding in such a setting.

options.text: Large teams with a high turnover

questions.explanation: The syllabus names geographic distance, outsourcing, and large teams with high turnover as obstacles to shared understanding — all three apply to the scenario described. Domain knowledge, mutual trust, and shared culture/values are enablers, not obstacles.

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's in-house digital services team collaborates closely and continuously with ground staff and passengers throughout QuickBag's development, using a product backlog of user stories and prototypes, with no external contractual delivery involved. Which of the following is **NOT** an accurate description of the "Participatory RE Process" configuration that this scenario exemplifies?

options.text: It is iterative, explorative, and customer-specific
Supplier and customer collaborate closely, with stakeholders strongly involved in both RE and development
It constitutes a fixed contractual basis for development by people with little stakeholder interaction after the requirements phase
Typical work products include a product backlog with user stories and/or task descriptions, and prototypes

questions.explanation: D describes the Contractual RE process (requirements as a binding contract, little stakeholder interaction afterward), not the Participatory RE process the scenario exemplifies, which is iterative, explorative, customer-specific, and built on close, continuous collaboration using backlogs and prototypes.
questions.reference: EU5.3 — Configuring a Requirements Engineering Process

questions.prompt: SkyHarbor's product owner needs a quick, low-effort way to prioritize a long list of newly requested QuickBag kiosk features before an upcoming sprint planning meeting, and the team agrees in advance to accept a single expert's judgment-based classification. Which of the following is **LEAST** consistent with the ad hoc prioritization techniques described in the syllabus?

options.text: Calculating a weighted score for each feature from multiple independently weighted assessment criteria such as cost, risk, and time to implement
Using MoSCoW (Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have this time)
Using Kano analysis, treating dissatisfiers as must-haves and delighters as could-/won't-haves
Using a Top-10 ranking based on expert judgment

questions.explanation: Calculating weighted scores from multiple independently weighted criteria is the defining characteristic of an *analytical* prioritization technique, not an ad hoc one. Top-10 ranking, MoSCoW, and Kano-based classification are all explicitly named ad hoc techniques.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about the RE principles, as applied to the QuickBag project, are TRUE, and which are FALSE?

statements.text: Because requirements will keep changing as SkyHarbor's operational needs evolve, the RE team should treat this volatility as an exceptional risk to be eliminated rather than as the normal case.

Even if passengers get exactly the kiosk features they explicitly asked for, QuickBag could still fail to delight them or gain a competitive edge, since innovation requires more than fulfilling stated wishes.
Validating the QuickBag requirements can safely be postponed until after the system has been fully deployed and is in daily operation.
A requirement's value is determined solely by its benefit, independent of the cost of eliciting, documenting, validating, and managing it.
Reusing the exact RE process that worked well for a previous airport kiosk project, without reflecting on whether it fits QuickBag's context, is consistent with systematic and disciplined work.

questions.explanation: Principle 7 treats changing requirements as the normal case, not an exceptional risk to eliminate (1, false). Principle 8 (Innovation) states that fully satisfying stated wishes is not enough to delight or gain competitive edge (2, true). Principle 6 requires validation to start during RE, not be postponed until after deployment (3, false). Principle 1 defines value as benefit minus cost, not benefit alone (4, false). Principle 9 explicitly warns against reusing past processes without reflecting on fit to the current context (5, false).

questions.prompt: NorthBridge's product owner writes the following statement for NorthBridge Open: "The onboarding platform must be built on the bank's existing cloud infrastructure provider because of an existing enterprise contract." According to the IREB classification of requirements, which kind of requirement is this?
questions.explanation: A requirement that limits the solution space beyond what is strictly necessary to meet functional and quality requirements — here, mandating a specific cloud provider because of an existing contract — is a constraint. It is not functional (no system behavior is described) and not a quality concern such as performance or security.

questions.prompt: During a joint workshop, a Requirements Engineer and the compliance officer sketch a simple box diagram on a whiteboard to clarify how the identity-document upload step relates to the sanctions-screening step. The sketch is photographed for reference and then erased once the discussion is reflected in the backlog. How should this work product be classified with respect to its life span?
questions.explanation: Temporary work products are created to support communication and shared understanding and are discarded after use; no metadata is kept. A baseline, by contrast, is a stable, change-controlled configuration — not a discarded sketch.
questions.reference: EU3.1 — Work Products in Requirements Engineering (Characteristics / Life Span)

questions.prompt: The national financial regulator mandates how long NorthBridge must retain KYC records and which identity checks are legally required. Per the typical stakeholder roles named in the syllabus, which role does the regulator play?
questions.explanation: The syllabus lists Users, Sponsors, Managers, Developers, Authorities, and Customers as typical stakeholder roles. A regulator that imposes legal requirements on the system is a textbook example of the Authority role.

questions.prompt: Name the TWO quality criteria below that the syllabus lists specifically for work products covering **multiple** requirements (rather than for a single requirement).
questions.explanation: The syllabus lists Consistent, Non-redundant, Complete, Modifiable, Traceable, and Conformant as quality criteria for work products covering multiple requirements. Verifiable, Unambiguous, Necessary, Understandable, and Adequate are quality criteria for a single requirement.
questions.reference: EU3.8 — Quality Criteria for Work Products and Requirements

questions.prompt: A compliance officer insists that every elicited requirement for NorthBridge Open be documented with full UML models — even a trivial requirement like "show a progress bar while the ID photo uploads" — arguing that "more documentation is always better." Which RE principle does this reasoning most directly violate?
questions.explanation: Value-orientation states that the value of a requirement equals its benefit minus the cost of eliciting, documenting, validating, and managing it; documenting trivial requirements exhaustively ignores this cost/benefit trade-off. Context and Systematic/disciplined work concern system boundaries and process adaptation, not documentation cost.

questions.prompt: Which TWO of the following are named in the syllabus as **enablers** of shared understanding between stakeholders, Requirements Engineers, and developers?

options.text: Domain knowledge shared by all parties
Outsourcing work to a new vendor

questions.explanation: The syllabus names domain knowledge, previous successful collaboration, shared culture and values, and mutual trust as enablers of shared understanding, while geographic distance, outsourcing, and large teams with high turnover are named as obstacles.

questions.prompt: In the NorthBridge requirements management tool, the KYC document-upload requirement shows status "reviewed" but not yet "validated." What is being tracked here?
questions.explanation: A life cycle model defines the allowed states (e.g., created, reviewed, validated) and transitions of a work product; tracking whether a requirement is "reviewed" but not "validated" is life cycle management, distinct from version numbers, configurations, or traceability links.

questions.prompt: NorthBridge wants to uncover requirements that the fraud/risk experts take so completely for granted that they never mention them in interviews (dissatisfiers). Name the TWO elicitation techniques best suited to this purpose, per the syllabus/handbook.
questions.explanation: Observation techniques (field observation and apprenticing) let the Requirements Engineer witness behavior stakeholders consider too obvious to mention, making them particularly suited to uncovering dissatisfiers. Interviews and questionnaires are questioning techniques that mainly surface conscious satisfiers.

questions.prompt: When NorthBridge Open first launched, an instant push notification confirming KYC approval was a novel feature customers did not ask for but loved once they discovered it. Today, every digital bank offers it, and customers would be upset if it were missing. According to the Kano model, this feature has evolved from a delighter into a:
questions.explanation: Per the Kano model's evolution over time, a delighter that becomes widely adopted and taken for granted turns into a dissatisfier: its absence now causes strong dissatisfaction, even though its presence is no longer noticed as special (the handbook illustrates this with the smartphone camera example).

questions.prompt: NorthBridge's vision document states "reduce onboarding time from 5 days to under 10 minutes," while a detailed requirement states "the OCR engine shall extract the ID-number field within 2 seconds." Should these two requirements be placed in the same paragraph of the system requirements specification?

options.text: Yes, abstraction level does not matter within a single document
No, high-level requirements should never appear in a system requirements specification
No, requirements at different abstraction levels should be kept separate by structuring the document accordingly
Yes, as long as both are in the same chapter

questions.explanation: The syllabus warns against mixing requirements at different abstraction levels within the same part of a work product; in large documents such as a system requirements specification, different abstraction levels should be kept separate through structuring.

questions.prompt: NorthBridge negotiates a fixed-price contract with an external supplier to build the entire KYC engine. The regulator requires a comprehensive, formally released requirements specification before coding starts, and there will be little stakeholder interaction with the supplier afterward. Which combination of RE process facets fits best?
questions.explanation: A fixed contractual basis, little ongoing stakeholder interaction after the requirements phase, and a regulator demanding an early, comprehensive, formally released specification are exactly the criteria for a Linear, Prescriptive, Customer-specific (Contractual) RE process.
questions.reference: EU5.3 — Configuring a Requirements Engineering Process

questions.prompt: Decide whether each of the following statements about quality criteria for RE work products is True or False.

statements.text: Adequacy and understandability are considered the most important quality criteria for a single requirement.
"Traceable" is listed as a quality criterion for a single requirement, not for a work product covering multiple requirements.
In a value-oriented approach, a low-value requirement does not need to fulfil every quality criterion to the same degree as a high-value requirement.
"Complete" has exactly the same meaning whether it is applied to a single requirement or to a work product covering multiple requirements.

questions.explanation: (1) The syllabus states adequacy and understandability are the most important criteria for a single requirement. (2) Traceable is a work-product-level criterion, not a single-requirement criterion. (3) Value-oriented RE scales quality-criteria rigor to a requirement's value. (4) "Complete" means something different for a single requirement (self-contained) than for a work product (no known relevant requirements missed).
questions.reference: EU3.8 — Quality Criteria for Work Products and Requirements

questions.prompt: Decide whether each of the following statements about resolving requirements conflicts is True or False.

statements.text: A value conflict is typically easier to resolve than a data conflict because values are flexible and change quickly.
Voting works best when there is a simple choice among a clearly understood set of alternatives.
Overruling is a suitable technique when there is ample time and all parties are willing to vote.
Definition of variants avoids introducing additional system complexity.
Agreement, unlike a compromise, means all stakeholders have reached their actually preferred option.

questions.explanation: (1) Values are described as stable and value conflicts as "notoriously difficult to resolve" — the opposite of easy. (2) Voting indeed works best for a simple, well-understood choice. (3) Overruling is typically used under time pressure when agreement/voting fail, not when there is ample time. (4) Definition of variants increases system complexity and cost. (5) Agreement means all parties reach their preferred option, while compromise means accepting a non-preferred but livable option.

questions.prompt: NorthBridge wants to specify that the platform reacts differently to a "resubmit ID photo" event depending on whether the application is currently in the state "Pending Document Check" or "Pending Manual Review." Which UML model type is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Requirements for state-dependent reactions to events are modeled with state machines (state machine diagrams in UML); activity diagrams model function/flow, class diagrams model structure/data, and use case diagrams model context.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is **NOT** one of the benefits of adequate RE listed in the syllabus?

options.text: Providing a basis for estimating development effort and cost
Guaranteeing zero cost overruns on every project
Reducing the risk of developing the wrong system

questions.explanation: The syllabus lists reducing risk, better problem understanding, and a basis for estimating effort/cost (plus being a prerequisite for testing) as the value RE adds — it never claims RE guarantees zero cost overruns, which is an unsupported, absolute claim.

questions.prompt: NorthBridge documents several requirements for the KYC platform. For each option, a requirement statement is followed by the functional-requirement aspect it is claimed to belong to (structure and data / function and flow / state and behavior). Name the THREE options where the match is **correct**.

options.text: "The system shall support 500 concurrent onboarding sessions." → structure and data
"The system shall encrypt all stored KYC documents using AES-256." → function and flow
"While the application is in the 'Pending Manual Review' state, the system shall disable automatic approval and route the case to a compliance officer." → state and behavior
"The system shall store the applicant's date of birth, nationality, and tax ID as part of the KYC profile." → structure and data
"The system shall first extract the ID number via OCR, then validate its checksum, then forward the result to the sanctions-screening service." → function and flow
"The onboarding platform shall be hosted exclusively within the EU to comply with data-residency law." → state and behavior

questions.explanation: (D) is correctly structure and data (persistent profile data). (E) is correctly function and flow (a sequence of actions). (C) is correctly state and behavior (a state-dependent reaction). (B) is actually a quality/security requirement, not function and flow; (A) is a quality/performance requirement, not structure and data; (F) is a constraint (legal/data-residency), not state and behavior.
questions.reference: EU3.1 — Aspects to be Considered in Work Products

questions.prompt: The product owner is preparing a prioritization session for the next sprint of the onboarding backlog. Name the TWO prioritization techniques explicitly listed as "ad hoc" techniques in the handbook.
questions.explanation: The handbook explicitly names Top-10 ranking and MoSCoW as common ad hoc prioritization techniques, based on expert judgment using a single, subjective criterion. Decision matrix and weighted multi-criteria scoring are analytical techniques; planning poker and formal AHP-style analysis are not ad hoc prioritization techniques described in this context.

questions.prompt: Because of audit requirements, NorthBridge's legal counsel insists that the risk-scoring requirements undergo a review led by an independent moderator, following a strict documented process with detailed checklists and a full audit trail, before sign-off. Which validation technique is being described?
questions.explanation: Inspections are led by an independent moderator (not the author), follow a strict documented process with checklists, and provide a detailed audit trail — making them suitable for safety-/regulation-critical release decisions. Walkthroughs are author-led and more informal; A/B testing and alpha testing are exploratory, not review, techniques.

questions.prompt: The compliance team and the engineering team both use the term "verification" — compliance means confirming a customer's identity against ID documents, engineering means confirming that software meets its specification. Which RE practice most directly addresses this risk of a homonym causing miscommunication?

options.text: Creating and maintaining a shared glossary

questions.explanation: A glossary is the central collection of definitions for context-specific terms and must mark homonyms (the same term used for different things) to prevent exactly this kind of miscommunication between compliance and engineering.

questions.prompt: Decide whether each statement about applying the nine RE principles to NorthBridge Open is True or False.

statements.text: Because onboarding requirements will keep changing as AML regulations evolve, this should be treated as an unfortunate exception to be eliminated as soon as possible.
Resolving a disagreement between the fraud team and the product team about risk-scoring thresholds is a core RE task related to the Stakeholders principle.
Defining the system boundary between the onboarding platform and the external sanctions-screening service is irrelevant to specifying good requirements.
Merely delivering exactly what customers explicitly asked for is sufficient to satisfy the Innovation principle.

A documented and agreed set of onboarding requirements represents explicit shared understanding, while team members' common assumptions about "how banks normally work" represent implicit shared understanding.

questions.explanation: (1) Evolution states that changing requirements are the normal case, not an accident to eliminate. (2) Resolving stakeholder disagreements is a core RE task under the Stakeholders principle. (3) Context explicitly requires understanding the system boundary and external interfaces. (4) Innovation means exceeding stated expectations, not merely satisfying them. (5) This correctly distinguishes explicit shared understanding (documented/agreed) from implicit shared understanding (shared assumptions/knowledge).

questions.prompt: Decide whether each of the following statements about requirements documents and documentation structures is True or False.

statements.text: A Stakeholder Requirements Specification is a subset of a User Requirements Specification.
A product backlog is an example of an "alternative documentation structure" rather than a classic requirements document.
The choice of documentation structure for NorthBridge Open should be independent of the chosen development process.
A story map is a frequently used alternative documentation structure, per the syllabus.

questions.explanation: (1) It is the reverse: a User Requirements Specification is a subset of a Stakeholder Requirements Specification. (2) Product backlogs are listed as an "alternative documentation structure." (3) The syllabus explicitly lists the chosen development process as one factor shaping documentation-structure choice. (4) Story maps are explicitly listed as a frequently used alternative documentation structure.
questions.reference: EU3.6 — Requirements Documents and Documentation Structures

questions.prompt: Name the TWO of the following validation techniques that are **LEAST** suitable to be classified as "exploratory techniques" — i.e., they actually belong to the "review techniques" category.
questions.explanation: Walkthroughs and Inspections are explicitly classified as review techniques. Beta testing, A/B testing, prototyping, and MVP building are explicitly classified as exploratory techniques, since they involve hands-on, dynamic use of an intermediate system version.

questions.prompt: Which field in the standard use-case form template captures the state of the system once a use case has completed unsuccessfully — for example, when the sanctions-screening check cannot complete due to a vendor outage?
questions.explanation: The use-case form template distinguishes "Success end condition" from "Failed end condition" — the latter captures the state reached when the use case execution fails, such as when an external service outage prevents sanctions screening from completing.

questions.prompt: A Requirements Engineer at NorthBridge wants a tool mainly to prioritize onboarding requirements, manage versions and configurations, and trace approved requirements forward to test cases. Which category of RE tool functionality best matches this need, per the syllabus?

options.text: Documentation of knowledge about the requirements

questions.explanation: Defining/storing attributes, prioritizing, managing versions/configurations, and tracking/tracing requirements are all explicitly listed under "management of requirements" tool support, distinct from managing the RE process, documenting knowledge, or modeling.

questions.prompt: Which THREE of the following are listed as natural-language pitfalls that should be used "with care" (rather than avoided outright) when writing NorthBridge's onboarding requirements?
questions.explanation: The syllabus lists passive voice, universal quantifiers, and nominalizations as things to be "used with care." Incomplete descriptions, unspecific nouns, incomplete conditions, and incomplete comparisons are listed as things to be avoided outright, a stricter category.

questions.prompt: NorthBridge studies its legacy paper-based KYC process manuals and the code of the old branch-teller system to identify detailed requirements for the new platform, even though the old system will be fully retired. Which elicitation technique is this?
questions.explanation: Extracting requirements from an existing (here: legacy/retiring) system's documentation, code, or other artifacts is system archaeology, an artifact-based gathering technique, distinct from apprenticing (participatory immersion) or field observation (watching current users).

questions.prompt: Before committing engineering resources, the onboarding team quickly assembles a clickable set of screens showing the document-upload flow, using a design tool, with real screens and click-through navigation but no real backend logic, to validate the flow with branch staff. Which kind of prototype is this?
questions.explanation: A medium-fidelity prototype using real screens and click-flows but no real functionality, used primarily to specify and validate the user interface, is a mock-up. A wireframe is lower fidelity (sketches), and a native prototype implements real functionality.

questions.prompt: Decide whether each statement about requirements traceability is True or False.

statements.text: Backward traceability is also known as pre-requirements-specification traceability.
Forward traceability answers the question "which stakeholder interview led to this requirement?"
Traceability "between requirements" can show that a user story is a refinement of a higher-level epic.
Explicit traceability can only be documented using specialized RE tools, never in plain documents.

questions.explanation: (1) Backward traceability is indeed also called pre-requirements-specification traceability. (2) That description matches backward, not forward, traceability. (3) Traceability between requirements explicitly covers refinement relationships such as an epic refined into user stories. (4) Explicit traceability can be documented in plain documents too (references, hyperlinks, matrices), not only via specialized tools.

questions.prompt: Which RE principle is most directly concerned with clarifying the system boundary and the external interfaces of NorthBridge Open?
questions.explanation: The Context principle states that systems cannot be understood in isolation and explicitly requires clarifying the system boundary and defining external interfaces — exactly the task described.

questions.prompt: Decide whether each statement about the appropriate level of detail for NorthBridge's onboarding requirements is True or False.

statements.text: The higher the cost of specifying a requirement in detail, the more detail should always be added, regardless of its value.
If rapid stakeholder feedback is available during design, a less detailed specification can suffice.
Regulatory constraints can force more detail than would otherwise be necessary.
A greater level of detail always reduces the total cost of a specification.
Low shared understanding between compliance and engineering calls for a more explicit, detailed specification.

questions.explanation: (1) Level of detail is a cost-vs-value trade-off, not an instruction to always add more detail. (2) Rapid feedback availability is explicitly listed as a factor reducing the need for detail. (3) Regulatory constraints are explicitly listed as a factor increasing required detail. (4) Greater detail increases, not reduces, specification cost. (5) Low shared understanding explicitly calls for more detailed, explicit specification.

questions.prompt: Elicitation, documentation, validation, and management are described in the syllabus as the major tasks of RE. Which of the following activities is explicitly stated to be **part of** elicitation, rather than a separate major task?
questions.explanation: The syllabus explicitly states that "requirements analysis and requirements conflict resolution are considered to be part of elicitation," distinguishing it from the separate major tasks of documentation, validation, and management.

questions.prompt: The team models "Applicant," "KYC Case," and "Risk Score" as classes with attributes and associations for the onboarding domain. Which UML diagram type is this?
questions.explanation: UML class diagrams specify classes, their attributes, and relationships — exactly what is being modeled here for Applicant, KYC Case, and Risk Score.

questions.prompt: The fraud team wants a stricter automated risk-rejection threshold, while the product team wants a looser threshold to reduce drop-off during onboarding — a classic interest conflict. Both sides have time to keep discussing, and they ultimately accept a middle-ground threshold that is not exactly what either team originally wanted, but that both can live with. Which conflict-resolution technique does this best describe?
questions.explanation: A compromise is an option that is not a party's original preference but that they can live with, reached because continuing the conflict is worse than accepting it — unlike an agreement, where the parties converge on an option they actually prefer.
questions.reference: EU4.3 — Resolving Conflicts Regarding Requirements (Resolution Techniques)

questions.prompt: NorthBridge's Requirements Engineers are deciding whether to model the KYC case lifecycle with UML diagrams or keep everything in natural language. Name the THREE correct **limitations** of requirements models, as stated in the syllabus.

options.text: A restricted modeling syntax reduces ambiguity
Most quality requirements and constraints cannot be expressed in models with reasonable effort
A legend is required only when using a non-standard modeling language
Models reduce the cognitive load of the reader by focusing on a single aspect
The restricted syntax of a graphical modeling language means not every relevant item of information can be expressed in a model
Keeping models that focus on different aspects consistent with each other is challenging
Relationships between requirements are easier to understand in models than in natural language

questions.explanation: The syllabus lists as limitations of models: difficulty keeping multi-aspect models consistent (F), models focusing mainly on functional requirements so quality/constraints are hard to express (B), and restricted syntax meaning not every relevant item can be expressed (E). Options A, C, D, and G describe advantages or conditions for using models, not limitations.
questions.reference: EU3.4 — The Role of Models in Requirements Engineering

questions.prompt: Name the TWO criteria that favor choosing an **explorative** RE process for a new NorthBridge Open feature (rather than a prescriptive one).

options.text: Stakeholders initially only have a vague idea of their requirements
Deadlines and cost take precedence over functionality and scope
Functionality and scope take precedence over cost and deadlines
The customer requires a fixed contract for system development
The development of the system may be tendered or outsourced

questions.explanation: The syllabus lists "stakeholders initially only have a vague idea about their requirements" and "deadlines and cost take precedence over functionality and scope" as criteria for an explorative process. The other options describe criteria favoring a prescriptive process instead.
questions.reference: EU5.2 — Requirements Engineering Process Facets (Purpose Facet)

questions.prompt: NorthBridge specifies a measurable quality requirement with the fields ID, Goal, Scale, Meter, Minimum, OK range, and Desired. Which of the following is **NOT** one of the fields of this form template?
questions.explanation: The form template for a measurable quality requirement contains ID, Goal, Scale, Meter, Minimum, OK range, and Desired. "Risk" is not part of this template; it is instead a requirements attribute used in requirements management (EU6.5).

questions.prompt: Name the TWO of the following that are **NOT** among the four categories into which "gathering techniques" are subdivided in the syllabus.
questions.explanation: Gathering techniques are subdivided into Questioning, Collaboration, Observation, and Artifact-based techniques. Creativity techniques and Design techniques are instead the two subcategories of design and idea-generating techniques.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is **NOT** one of the properties of a requirements configuration, per the syllabus?
questions.explanation: The syllabus lists Logical connection, Consistency, Uniqueness, Unchangeability, and Basis for reset as properties of a requirements configuration. "Volatility" is not one of them — a configuration is by definition unchangeable, the opposite of volatile.

questions.prompt: Decide whether each statement about documenting NorthBridge's onboarding requirements is True or False.

statements.text: Avoiding redundancy means referencing content instead of repeating it across multiple work products.
It is best practice to decide which work products will be used only after most elicitation is complete, to avoid wasted planning effort.
When different aspects of a requirement are documented in separate work products, those work products do not need to be kept consistent with each other.
Selecting a work product type that fits its intended purpose is one of the syllabus's general documentation guidelines.

questions.explanation: (1) Avoiding redundancy via referencing is an explicit general documentation guideline. (2) Work products should be planned at an early stage of the project, not after elicitation is mostly done. (3) Work products covering different aspects must be kept consistent with each other, not left inconsistent. (4) Selecting a fitting work product type is explicitly listed as a general documentation guideline.
questions.reference: EU3.1 — General Documentation Guidelines / Plan the Work Products to be Used

questions.prompt: NorthBridge Bank's project team is compiling the information base for NorthBridge Open. Which of the following is the most appropriate classification of "the national Anti-Money-Laundering regulation mandating identity verification before an account can be activated" as a requirements source?
questions.explanation: Documented sources comprise laws, regulations, standards, contracts and other written material that informs or constrains requirements; a national AML regulation is exactly that. It is not a systematic source (an existing system/legacy application), a human source (a stakeholder who can be interviewed), or a model.

questions.prompt: During elicitation for NorthBridge Open, the compliance officer insists every applicant's address must be verified by postal mail (adding 5 business days), while the product owner insists the end-to-end onboarding must complete within 10 minutes to stay competitive. Both positions are explicitly documented, and neither side disputes the facts or terminology involved — they simply want the requirement itself to say something different. Which conflict type does this best illustrate?
questions.explanation: A subject matter conflict exists when stakeholders disagree about the actual content of a requirement itself (what it should state), which is the case here — both sides agree on the facts and the terms used, they just want the requirement's content to differ. It is not a data conflict (disagreement about underlying facts/data), relationship conflict (personal/interpersonal friction), or structural conflict (disagreement about how requirements are organized/structured).
questions.reference: EU4.3 — Resolving Conflicts regarding Requirements (Conflict Types)

questions.prompt: NorthBridge must host all onboarding data exclusively within approved national data centers because of a data-residency law. Which category of constraint, per the handbook, is this?
questions.explanation: Restrictions imposed by laws, contracts, standards, or regulations are classified as legal constraints — a data-residency law is a textbook example. Technical constraints concern interfaces/frameworks; organizational concerns structures/processes; cultural concerns user habits shaped by culture.
questions.reference: EU3.1 — Aspects to be Considered in Work Products (Constraints)

questions.prompt: Name the TWO fields below that actually belong to the standard use-case form template.
questions.explanation: "Primary actor" and "Trigger" are genuine fields of the standard use-case form template (alongside Name, Precondition, Success/Failed end condition, Other actors, Normal flow, Alternate flows, Extensions, Related information). Risk rating, story points, business value, and sprint number are backlog/attribute concepts, not use-case template fields.

questions.prompt: Decide whether each statement about handling changes to NorthBridge's onboarding requirements is True or False.

statements.text: While a requirement is still in draft state, its author may change it without following a formal change process.
In NorthBridge's agile onboarding squad, the product owner typically acts as the change authority for backlog items.
In the linear, contractual part of the KYC program, change requests are typically decided by a Change Control Board.
A standard, pre-authorized, low-risk change — such as updating a displayed VAT percentage — still requires the same lengthy approval process as an emergency change.
Once a requirement is implemented in the live onboarding system, changes to it no longer need an impact analysis.

questions.explanation: (1) An author may freely change a requirement while it is still a draft. (2) In an iterative approach, the product owner typically acts as change authority. (3) In a linear approach, a Change Control Board typically decides. (4) Standard changes are pre-authorized and low-risk, precisely so they do NOT need the same lengthy process as other changes. (5) An impact analysis is always needed once a requirement is implemented operationally, since changes now affect users and business processes.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is **NOT** one of the five recommended steps for configuring an RE process, per the syllabus?
questions.explanation: The syllabus's five-step procedure for configuring an RE process is: analyze influencing factors, assess facet criteria, configure the process, determine work products, and select appropriate practices. "Hire additional developers" is not part of this procedure.
questions.reference: EU5.3 — Configuring a Requirements Engineering Process

mocks.title: "Lakeview General Hospital" Outpatient Appointment & Patient-Portal System

questions.prompt: During a kickoff workshop, a Requirements Engineer sketches a rough interaction flow on a whiteboard purely to help scheduling staff and developers agree on how a patient would search for an open slot. The sketch is photographed for reference and then erased, with no metadata or revision history kept. According to the syllabus's classification of work product life spans, this sketch is best described as a:
questions.explanation: A sketch created only to support communication in a workshop, discarded afterward with no metadata kept, is the definition of a temporary work product. Evolving and durable work products require at least some retained metadata and, for durable products, a baseline or release.

questions.prompt: A draft statement for Lakeview Connect reads: "The system shall store all patient appointment data exclusively on servers located within national borders, per the Ministry of Health's data-residency regulation." Which kind of requirement, per the syllabus's classification, does this best represent?
questions.explanation: A legally mandated data-residency rule restricts the solution space (where data may be stored) beyond what is strictly necessary to satisfy functional or quality requirements, which is the definition of a constraint. It does not describe a system behavior (functional) or a quality attribute like performance or security.

questions.prompt: Ingrid Voss, Lakeview General Hospital's Data Protection Officer, reviews the Lakeview Connect requirements to ensure compliance with national health-data regulation, even though she will never personally book or manage appointments through the system. Which typical stakeholder role, per the syllabus, best fits Ingrid's involvement?
questions.explanation: The syllabus lists "Authorities" as a typical stakeholder role for parties who impose rules or regulations on a system without using it or paying for it, which fits a Data Protection Officer enforcing regulatory compliance. She is not a user, sponsor, developer, or customer in this context.

questions.prompt: During requirements workshops, scheduling supervisor Tomas Reyes insists that walk-in patients must be accommodated within the same booking slots that clinicians want reserved exclusively for follow-up visits. Both parties are adamant, and the Requirements Engineer must identify and work toward reconciling their differing needs. Which fundamental RE principle is most directly illustrated by this task?
questions.explanation: Principle 2 states that stakeholders may have different needs and viewpoints resulting in conflicting requirements, and that identifying and resolving such conflicts is a task of RE. Value-orientation, validation, and innovation are distinct principles not centered on reconciling differing stakeholder needs.

questions.prompt: Name the three factors that, according to the syllabus, should influence how much detail is used when specifying the requirement "Lakeview Connect shall let patients upload referral documents before an appointment."

options.text: Regulatory constraints on how patient-submitted medical documents must be handled
Cost of producing a highly detailed specification versus the value it creates
Availability of rapid stakeholder feedback from scheduling staff during design
The personal handwriting style of the Requirements Engineer who drafts the requirement
Whether the scheduling supervisor prefers a formal or informal writing style
The brand of document-scanning hardware used in the IT department's test lab

questions.explanation: The syllabus lists availability of rapid stakeholder feedback, regulatory/standards constraints, and the cost-versus-value trade-off among the factors influencing level of detail. The RE's handwriting style, scanner hardware brand, and personal writing-style preference are not among the listed factors.

questions.prompt: The hospital's quality manager asks for a report showing, for each hospital department, the total number of appointment requests logged through Lakeview Connect last month. Which type of view, per the syllabus, does this report represent?
questions.explanation: Summaries, totals, or averages calculated across a set of requirements (here, counts per department) define an aggregating view. A selective view would filter to a subset of requirements without summarizing, and a projective view would show only selected attributes of each requirement.

questions.prompt: In the Lakeview Connect system requirements specification, a Requirements Engineer writes, in the same short subsection: "REQ-114: The appointment confirmation screen shall display the clinician's name in 12-point bold font." immediately followed by "REQ-115: The hospital shall reduce average patient no-show rates while maintaining current staffing levels." What documentation problem does this illustrate?

options.text: A violation of the non-redundancy criterion
Confusing a constraint with a quality requirement
Mixing requirements from different abstraction levels within the same part of the document

questions.explanation: REQ-114 is a very detailed, low-level requirement while REQ-115 is a high-level business goal; placing them in the same small subsection mixes abstraction levels, which the syllabus explicitly warns against, especially within small/medium-sized sections. This is not primarily a redundancy, constraint-labeling, or traceability issue.

questions.prompt: For each described disagreement among Lakeview Connect stakeholders, judge whether the stated conflict-type classification is TRUE or FALSE.

statements.text: Scheduling staff and clinicians disagree because one group trusts last year's no-show statistics from one source while the other group relies on a different, inconsistent report — this is a data conflict.

Cardiology clinicians insist appointment slots must be 30 minutes because of a national clinical-safety rule that cannot be changed, while dermatology clinicians need only 10-minute slots under a different applicable guideline — this is a subject matter conflict.

A scheduling clerk and a nurse keep arguing about unrelated portal requirements mainly because of long-standing personal friction from an unrelated incident last year — this is classified as an interest conflict.
Hospital IT wants sole control over which features reach production because it owns the only deployment pipeline, creating a power imbalance with the product owner — this is a structural conflict.

The product owner wants to launch extra convenience features quickly for patient satisfaction, while the finance manager wants to minimize build cost, reflecting different role-based goals — this is an interest conflict.

questions.explanation: (1) Differing trust in inconsistent data sources is the definition of a data conflict. (2) Differing factual needs rooted in different, unchangeable national rules is a subject matter conflict. (3) The scenario describes negative past experience and emotion driving the argument, which is a relationship conflict, not an interest conflict — so statement 3 is false. (4) Power imbalance from exclusive control of a resource (the pipeline) is a structural conflict. (5) Differing role-based goals (patient satisfaction vs. cost control) is an interest conflict.

questions.prompt: Lakeview General Hospital commissions an external software supplier to build the entire Lakeview Connect system. The hospital's legal department insists on a fixed-price contract based on a comprehensive, formally released system requirements specification, with only limited stakeholder availability once development starts. Which typical RE process configuration, per the syllabus, best fits this situation?
questions.explanation: A fixed contract based on a comprehensive, formally released specification with little ongoing stakeholder interaction is the defining case for the Contractual RE Process (typically linear, prescriptive, customer-specific). The Participatory and Product-Oriented configurations both assume continuous stakeholder involvement, which is explicitly ruled out here.
questions.reference: EU5.3 — Configuring a Requirements Engineering Process

questions.prompt: Lakeview Connect's documentation team is deciding which aspects to cover when specifying the appointment-booking requirements. Judge each statement as TRUE or FALSE.

statements.text: Every single work product must simultaneously document functional requirements, quality requirements, and constraints in full detail.
A patient's request to reschedule an appointment (a context-related event) may trigger a state transition in the appointment's status (a state-and-behavior aspect).
Requirements models typically focus on one aspect, such as structure and data, while abstracting from other aspects such as quality.
Because a context diagram and a class diagram for the same system cover different aspects, they never need to be kept consistent with each other.
"Structure and data" and "function and flow" are both examples of aspects that fall under functional requirements.

questions.explanation: (1) Not every work product must cover all three kinds in full detail; some work products, especially models, deliberately focus on one aspect. (2) This is exactly the kind of interrelationship the syllabus describes between context, state/behavior, function/flow, and data aspects. (3) Models typically abstract from other aspects to reduce cognitive load. (4) Work products or chapters documenting different aspects must still be kept consistent with each other, so statement 4 is false. (5) Structure/data and function/flow are explicitly listed as aspects of functional requirements.
questions.reference: EU3.1.4 — Aspects to be Considered in Work Products

questions.prompt: Lakeview General Hospital's legacy phone-booking process suffered from chronic scheduling errors. Judge each statement about typical causes of inadequate Requirements Engineering as TRUE or FALSE.

statements.text: Rushing straight into building a solution before understanding stakeholder needs is a typical cause of inadequate RE.
Assuming that requirements are self-evident reduces the risk of inadequate RE.
Communication problems between scheduling staff, clinicians, and the IT department can lead to missing or incorrect requirements.
Inadequate RE education and skills among the project team are unrelated to the quality of elicited requirements.

questions.explanation: (1) Rushing into building is explicitly listed as a cause of inadequate RE. (2) Assuming requirements are self-evident is itself listed as a cause of inadequate RE, not a mitigation, so statement 2 is false. (3) Communication problems between involved parties are explicitly listed as a cause. (4) Inadequate RE education and skills are explicitly listed as a cause, so claiming they are "unrelated" is false.

questions.prompt: During elicitation, patients never explicitly ask for it, yet user research shows that if Lakeview Connect did not let patients view their past appointment history at all, patients would be outraged and consider the system unusable. According to the Kano model, this feature is best classified as a:
questions.explanation: A feature that patients do not explicitly request but would be extremely unhappy to find missing is a dissatisfier (basic factor), per the Kano model. A delighter would be an unexpected feature that excites users when present but causes no complaint when absent, and a satisfier is explicitly requested and scales with satisfaction.

questions.prompt: A draft requirement for Lakeview Connect reads: "The system shall notify the appropriate staff when a high-risk patient misses an appointment." Which natural-language pitfall does the phrase "the appropriate staff" illustrate?
questions.explanation: "The appropriate staff" does not specify which role or person should be notified, making it an unspecific noun — a pitfall the syllabus explicitly lists as something to avoid. It is not an incomplete comparison, incomplete condition, universal quantifier, or nominalization.

questions.prompt: Judge each of the following statements about Principle 6 (Validation) as TRUE or FALSE, in the context of validating Lakeview Connect requirements before development starts.

statements.text: Validation must wait until the system has been deployed, since only real patients can judge whether their needs are met.
Checking whether agreement about the requirements has been achieved among stakeholders such as clinicians and scheduling staff is part of validation.
Validation includes checking whether context assumptions, such as "every patient has reliable internet access," are reasonable.
Once a requirement has been documented in natural language, it is automatically considered validated.

questions.explanation: (1) Principle 6 requires validation to start already during RE, not be postponed until after deployment, so statement 1 is false. (2) Checking stakeholder agreement is explicitly one of the things validation must verify. (3) Checking the reasonableness of context assumptions is explicitly part of validation. (4) Documenting a requirement in natural language does not by itself validate it — validation is a separate, deliberate activity, so statement 4 is false.

questions.prompt: Consider the draft requirement: "The system shall be faster and shall never lose appointment data." Name the two natural-language pitfalls that this sentence illustrates.

options.text: Incomplete comparison ("faster" without stating faster than what)

questions.explanation: "Faster" is an incomplete comparison because no baseline is given ("faster than what?"), and "never" is a universal quantifier, both explicitly listed as pitfalls/care items in the syllabus. The sentence is active voice, contains no nominalization, and is not simply an "incomplete description" in the syllabus's specific sense.

questions.prompt: Name the three design and idea-generating techniques that the Lakeview Connect team could use to come up with innovative portal features, as opposed to gathering techniques.

options.text: A brainstorming workshop with clinicians and patients
Storyboarding a patient's journey from symptom onset to follow-up visit
