A structured interview with the scheduling supervisor
Observing front-desk staff during a busy clinic morning
Reviewing the hospital's existing paper appointment forms
Building low-fidelity mock-ups to explore new booking flows

questions.explanation: Brainstorming, storyboards, and prototyping (e.g., mock-ups) are explicitly named as design and idea-generating techniques intended to stimulate creativity. Interviews, observation, and artifact review are gathering techniques (questioning, observation, and artifact-based techniques respectively), not design/idea-generating techniques.

questions.prompt: Judge each statement about managing the Lakeview Connect requirements as TRUE or FALSE.

statements.text: A version number for a work product typically consists of at least two parts: the version and the increment.
Version control makes it possible to restore an earlier version of a requirements document after an unwanted change.
A requirements configuration may legitimately contain two different versions of the same work product at once, as long as both are recent.
A baseline is, by definition, a configuration that remains open to uncontrolled, ad-hoc changes by any team member.
Keeping a documented history of what was changed is one of the measures required for version control.

questions.explanation: (1) A version number typically has at least a version and an increment part. (2) Restoring an earlier version is an explicit purpose of version control. (3) A configuration contains at most one version of each work product, so statement 3 is false. (4) A baseline is, by definition, stable and change-controlled, so claiming it stays open to ad-hoc change is false. (5) A history of what was changed is one of the three required measures for version control.

questions.prompt: Which EARS phrase template best fits the following Lakeview Connect requirement? "WHEN a patient cancels an appointment less than two hours before its scheduled time, the system shall release the slot to the stand-by waiting list."
questions.explanation: The sentence follows the EARS structure "WHEN `<trigger>` the `<system>` shall `<response>`," which defines the event-driven template, triggered here by the patient's late cancellation. It is not a ubiquitous requirement (which has no trigger), an unwanted-behavior requirement (which uses "IF...THEN"), a state-driven requirement (which uses "WHILE"), or an optional-feature requirement (which uses "WHERE").

questions.prompt: Hospital IT lead Ben Okafor wants to select an RE tool for managing Lakeview Connect's requirements before the team has agreed on any RE procedures or responsibilities. Which statement correctly identifies the problem with this plan, per the syllabus's guidance on introducing RE tools?

options.text: RE tools should always be selected before any RE process is defined, so the process can be shaped around the tool
License cost is the only life-cycle cost that matters when selecting a tool
An appropriate tool can only be sought once proper RE procedures and responsibilities have been established
Pilot projects should be avoided because they delay tool rollout

questions.explanation: The syllabus states that an appropriate tool can only be sought once proper RE procedures and techniques have been introduced, and that tool introduction requires clear RE responsibilities and procedures — selecting a tool first inverts this order. Life-cycle costs beyond licensing, and the use of pilot projects, are both explicitly recommended, contradicting options C and D.

questions.prompt: To understand where front-desk staff currently struggle, a Requirements Engineer spends a full morning quietly watching scheduling clerks handle phone calls and walk-ins at Lakeview General Hospital, without interrupting them. Which category of gathering technique is this?
questions.explanation: Quietly watching staff perform their work without interrupting them is the defining characteristic of an observation technique, one of the four categories of gathering techniques. It is not a questioning technique (which involves asking), a collaboration technique (which involves joint activity), or an artifact-based technique (which involves reviewing existing documents/systems).

questions.prompt: A product backlog item for Lakeview Connect reads: "As a scheduling clerk, I want to filter appointments by clinic location." Judged against Cohn's classic phrase template for user stories, what is missing?
questions.explanation: Cohn's template is "As a `<role>`, I want `<requirement>`, so that `<benefit>`." The example states a role and a requirement but omits the benefit clause explaining why the filter is needed. Acceptance criteria are a recommended addition to user stories but are not part of the three-part phrase template itself.

questions.prompt: Name the three reasons, among those explicitly listed under Principle 7 (Evolution), that are genuine causes for requirements to change over the course of the Lakeview Connect project.

options.text: The Requirements Engineer rewrites the glossary using a different font
A new national e-health data-protection regulation comes into force mid-project
Patients using an early release ask for a new self-check-in feature
The scheduling team migrates from spreadsheets to a new requirements management tool
The hospital's referral process changes after merging with a partner clinic network
The hospital's quality manager reformats the requirements document template

questions.explanation: Changes in laws/regulations, feedback from users after using a system, and changed business processes are all explicitly listed as reasons requirements evolve. Rewriting a glossary's font, migrating tools, and reformatting a document template are administrative/tooling actions, not listed causes of requirements change.

questions.prompt: The Lakeview Connect team is setting up a project glossary. Judge each statement as TRUE or FALSE.

statements.text: The glossary should be maintained by a single responsible person or a small group, not updated ad hoc by everyone.
Using the glossary should be optional, so that experienced clinicians are not forced to use the agreed terminology.
Synonyms, such as "patient portal" and "patient self-service site" referring to the same thing, should be marked as such.
Homonyms, such as the term "slot" meaning both an appointment time and a parking space in facility-management documents, should be actively encouraged to keep the glossary short.
The glossary only needs to be created once, at the start of the project, and requires no further maintenance afterward.

questions.explanation: (1) The syllabus requires defining a person or small group responsible for the glossary. (2) Glossary use must be made mandatory, so calling it "optional" is false. (3) Synonyms should indeed be marked as such. (4) Homonyms should be avoided or marked, not encouraged, so statement 4 is false. (5) The glossary must be maintained over the entire course of system development, so claiming no further maintenance is needed is false.

questions.prompt: The hospital's marketing lead wants Lakeview Connect to prominently advertise elective cosmetic procedures on the booking homepage, viewing this as good for revenue, while a group of clinicians object on the grounds that a clinical appointment system should never resemble a sales platform — a principle they hold deeply and will not compromise on. Which conflict type best fits this disagreement?
questions.explanation: A deeply held, stable principle ("a clinical system should never resemble a sales platform") that the clinicians refuse to compromise on is characteristic of a value conflict, which is more individual and long-term than an interest conflict based on shifting positions or goals. It is not based on inconsistent data, nor on power imbalance or resource dependency (structural conflict).

questions.prompt: In Cockburn's use case form template, which field captures the event that initiates execution of a "Book Appointment" use case, such as a patient clicking "Find a Slot"?
questions.explanation: The "Trigger" field in Cockburn's use case form template is defined as the event that initiates execution of the use case. "Precondition" describes conditions that must already hold, "Primary actor" names who performs the use case, and "Success end condition" describes the resulting state after successful completion.
questions.reference: EU3.3 — Template-Based Work Products (Use Case Form Template)

questions.prompt: Because clinicians at Lakeview General Hospital can spare only a single hour per month for requirements workshops due to patient-care duties, the Requirements Engineer concludes that a process built on continuous stakeholder feedback loops is not feasible. Which influencing factor is primarily driving this conclusion?

options.text: Complexity and criticality of the system

questions.explanation: The scenario centers on how much time and access clinicians can provide, which is precisely the "capability and availability of stakeholders" influencing factor; limited availability rules out processes built on continuous feedback. Requirements volatility, overall process fit, and system complexity/criticality are separate influencing factors not described here.

questions.prompt: Lakeview Connect is being developed with short, iterative releases and a continuously evolving set of patient-portal features. Name the two documentation structures that would be **LEAST** suitable as the primary way to organize these evolving requirements.
questions.explanation: A Business Requirements Specification and a Stakeholder Requirements Specification are comprehensive, typically upfront documents associated with linear/contractual settings, making them least suitable as the primary structure for a continuously evolving, iterative project. Product backlogs, sprint backlogs, and (to a lesser extent) vision documents are the documentation structures the syllabus associates with iterative, agile work.
questions.reference: EU3.6 — Requirements Documents and Documentation Structures

questions.prompt: Judge each statement about eliciting and validating Lakeview Connect requirements as TRUE or FALSE.

statements.text: Quality requirements and constraints are elicited just as naturally as functional requirements, so stakeholders rarely need prompting to mention them.
A standard such as ISO 25010 can be used as a checklist to help elicit quality requirements, such as the portal's required availability during clinic hours.
Constraints can be uncovered by considering restrictions on the solution space, such as legal, organizational, or technical limitations.
The best elicitation results are usually achieved by selecting a single elicitation technique and applying it exhaustively to every stakeholder.
Which elicitation technique is appropriate depends on factors such as the type of system, the development life cycle, and the people involved.

questions.explanation: (1) The syllabus notes stakeholders tend to omit quality requirements and constraints because they take them for granted, so statement 1 is false. (2) ISO 25010 is explicitly recommended as a checklist for eliciting quality requirements. (3) Constraints are explicitly found by considering restrictions on the solution space. (4) The syllabus states the best results are usually achieved by combining different elicitation techniques, not relying on just one, so statement 4 is false. (5) Picking the right technique explicitly depends on system type, life cycle model, and people involved.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is **NOT** one of the categories the syllabus uses to classify where requirements can occur?
questions.explanation: The syllabus's five categories for where requirements occur are system, stakeholder, user, domain, and business requirements. "Acceptance requirements" is not one of these listed categories.

questions.prompt: The Requirements Engineer needs to specify how an appointment moves between the states Requested, Confirmed, Checked-In, Completed, and Cancelled, including which events trigger each transition. Which model type is best suited for this?
questions.explanation: Specifying states, the events that trigger transitions between them, and associated actions is exactly what state machines/statecharts (expressed as UML state machine diagrams) are designed for. A class diagram models structure/data, an activity diagram models function/flow, and a context diagram models the system's surrounding actors, not internal state transitions.

questions.prompt: An auditor asks the Lakeview Connect team to show which test case verifies REQ-203 ("the system shall log every access to a patient's medical history") and which stakeholder request originally led to this requirement. Providing hyperlinked references between the requirement, its origin, and the test case is an example of:
questions.explanation: Documenting traceability using explicit links (here, hyperlinks) between a requirement, its origin, and a downstream test case is the definition of explicit traceability. Implicit traceability instead relies on structuring/naming conventions without explicit references, and this is not a view or a baseline.

questions.prompt: After analyzing a persistent disagreement between cardiology and dermatology clinicians about slot duration, the Requirements Engineer proposes offering each specialty its own configurable default slot length within the same system, so both can be accommodated without forcing one group to concede. Which conflict resolution technique is being applied?
questions.explanation: Offering each group its own variant (a configurable default per specialty) so that both parties' needs are met without concession is the definition of "definition of variants." It differs from compromise (each side gives something up to meet in the middle), voting, overruling, and agreement.

questions.prompt: A Requirements Engineer wants a UML diagram that shows the Lakeview Connect system together with the actors Patient, Scheduling Clerk, and Clinician, and the use cases through which each actor interacts with the system (e.g., Book Appointment, Reschedule Appointment, View Patient Record). Which UML model type should be used?
questions.explanation: UML use case diagrams model a system and its context in terms of actors and the use cases through which they interact with the system, exactly as described. Class diagrams model structure/data, sequence diagrams model object interaction over time, and activity diagrams model function/flow rather than actor-system interaction overview.

questions.prompt: A requirement in the Lakeview Connect specification states: "The appointment-booking screen shall respond quickly when a patient searches for available slots." Which single-requirement quality criterion is most clearly violated?
questions.explanation: Verifiable means fulfillment of the requirement can be objectively checked, e.g. by test or measurement. "Quickly" has no quantified threshold (such as a maximum response time in seconds), so there is no way to verify compliance. The requirement may still be necessary and adequate, and completeness concerns missing content rather than vague phrasing.
questions.reference: EU3.8 — Quality Criteria for Work Products and Requirements

questions.prompt: The Lakeview Connect system requirements specification is being reviewed as a whole document. Name the three quality criteria that apply specifically to work products covering multiple requirements, rather than to a single requirement.
questions.explanation: Consistent, traceable, and non-redundant are explicitly listed as quality criteria for work products covering multiple requirements. Verifiable, understandable, and adequate are quality criteria for single requirements, not for the work product as a whole.
questions.reference: EU3.8 — Quality Criteria for Work Products and Requirements

questions.prompt: Name the three important aspects of requirements validation that the Lakeview Connect team should apply before freezing the system requirements specification for development.

options.text: Validating the specification only once, right before go-live
Keeping the identification of defects separate from their correction during the same review session
Validating the specification from different views, such as a patient-safety view and a data-protection view
Involving the right stakeholders, such as both scheduling staff and clinicians, not only hospital IT
Automating validation entirely so that no human review is required

questions.explanation: Involving the right stakeholders, separating defect identification from correction, and validating from different views are three of the four aspects the syllabus explicitly names for requirements validation (the fourth being repeated validation). Automating validation entirely and validating only once both contradict the syllabus's guidance.

questions.prompt: While drafting a context diagram for Lakeview Connect, the team cannot agree on whether the hospital's existing Electronic Health Record (EHR) system should be drawn as an external actor in the context or treated as part of the system under development. This disagreement is primarily about defining the:
questions.explanation: Deciding whether an element (the EHR system) is part of the system being developed or part of its surrounding context is exactly the definition of clarifying the system boundary, which the syllabus names as a genuine, sometimes-evolving RE task. The context boundary instead separates the RE-relevant environment from the rest of the world, which is not the issue described.

questions.prompt: Name the two correct statements about handling a request to change an already-baselined Lakeview Connect requirement.

options.text: In a linear, plan-driven setting, the decision on the change is often taken by a Change Control Board
A Change Advisory Board exists only to handle change requests initiated directly by patients
In a more iterative approach, the product owner can add the change as a new backlog item and prioritize it accordingly
Requirement changes should always be rejected once a work product has been baselined, to preserve stability
Changes only ever need to be handled if they originate from external regulators

questions.explanation: The syllabus states that in a linear/plan-driven approach, change decisions are often taken by a Change Control Board, while in an iterative approach, the product owner adds the change to the backlog and prioritizes it. Rejecting all changes after baselining, limiting handling to regulator-driven changes, and restricting a Change Advisory Board to patient-initiated requests all contradict or overstate the syllabus's description.

questions.prompt: Consider the following draft requirement for Lakeview Connect: "REQ-77: The system shall send a reminder notification to the patient." For each statement about this requirement's quality, judge TRUE or FALSE.

statements.text: The requirement is unambiguous, because "reminder notification" clearly specifies the channel (SMS, email, or push) and timing.
The requirement is verifiable, because testers can indisputably check whether a notification was sent, even without first agreeing on timing and channel.
The requirement could still be adequate even though it is incomplete, if it genuinely reflects an agreed stakeholder need captured elsewhere.
If this requirement does not contribute to any stakeholder goal, it fails the "necessary" criterion regardless of how well it is worded.
Understandability only matters if the requirement will later be formally tested.

questions.explanation: (1) The requirement does not specify channel or timing, so it is ambiguous, not unambiguous — statement 1 is false. (2) Because channel and timing are undefined, fulfillment cannot be checked indisputably, so it is not currently verifiable — statement 2 is false. (3) Adequacy concerns whether a requirement reflects a true, agreed need, which is independent of completeness, so statement 3 is true. (4) Necessity requires contributing to a stakeholder goal; failing to do so fails this criterion regardless of wording quality, so statement 4 is true. (5) Understandability is one of the two most important criteria and matters regardless of whether formal testing follows, so statement 5 is false.
questions.reference: EU3.8 — Quality Criteria for Work Products and Requirements

questions.prompt: Before releasing the final, milestone version of the Lakeview Connect system requirements specification — which carries significant patient-safety risk — the hospital wants a validation technique with an independent moderator, pre-meeting individual preparation guided by checklists, and a documented audit trail of defects found. Which review technique is being described?
questions.explanation: An independent moderator, individual pre-meeting preparation guided by checklists, and a documented audit trail of defects are the hallmarks of an inspection, the most formal review technique, typically used for milestone or high-risk work products. A walkthrough is led by the author rather than an independent moderator and is less formally documented.

questions.prompt: The Lakeview Connect team models the domain concepts Patient, Appointment, and Clinician. Each Appointment is booked by exactly one Patient and assigned to exactly one Clinician; a Patient may have many Appointments over time, but each Appointment belongs to only one Patient. Which UML class diagram relationship correctly expresses the Patient–Appointment connection?

options.text: A generalization of Appointment from Patient
A one-to-many association between Patient and Appointment, with Patient on the "one" side
A one-to-one association between Patient and Appointment
A many-to-many association between Patient and Appointment

questions.explanation: Since one Patient can have many Appointments but each Appointment belongs to exactly one Patient, this is a one-to-many association with Patient on the "one" side — the standard way to express such a relationship in a UML class diagram. One-to-one, many-to-many, and generalization relationships would misrepresent the stated cardinalities.

questions.prompt: Name the two correct heuristic statements about combining RE process facets.

options.text: Linear and prescriptive facets are frequently chosen together
Linear RE processes require only minimal validation, since requirements are fixed up front
The market-oriented facet combines well with the linear and prescriptive facets
A linear RE process works well even without any process for changing requirements
Explorative RE processes are typically also iterative processes

questions.explanation: The syllabus's hints explicitly state that linear and prescriptive facets are frequently chosen together, and that explorative RE processes are typically also iterative ones. It also explicitly states that the market-oriented facet does *not* combine well with linear and prescriptive facets, and that linear processes require intensive validation and a sophisticated change process — contradicting the other two options.

questions.prompt: Name the two correct statements about using UML activity diagrams to specify the Lakeview Connect appointment-booking process.

options.text: Activity diagrams can show which actor (e.g., patient vs. scheduling clerk) is responsible for each action in the booking process
Activity diagrams primarily specify static structural relationships between domain objects, such as class attributes
At CPRE Foundation Level, UML activity diagrams can be used to model both system functions and business/technical processes
An activity diagram can fully and precisely express quality requirements, such as a maximum two-second response time
Activity diagrams are used to model the actors surrounding a system and its external interfaces, replacing context diagrams

questions.explanation: UML activity diagrams can express who (which actor) is responsible for each action, and at CPRE Foundation Level they are used both for system functions and for business/technical process modeling. Modeling surrounding actors and interfaces is the role of context models, static structural relationships belong to class diagrams, and models generally cannot express quality requirements with reasonable effort.

questions.prompt: Name the two auxiliary techniques that the Requirements Engineer could use to help structure a discussion about whether to adopt a disputed feature for the Lakeview Connect portal.
questions.explanation: Consider-all-facts and decision matrix are explicitly listed as auxiliary techniques that support structuring a conflict discussion. Voting, overruling, and agreement are listed as the main conflict resolution techniques, not auxiliary ones.

questions.prompt: Judge each statement about prioritizing Lakeview Connect requirements as TRUE or FALSE.

statements.text: Ad hoc prioritization techniques, such as MoSCoW, rely on expert judgment and typically a single, subjective criterion.
Prioritization should always be based on a single fixed criterion, since using multiple criteria makes results incomparable.

If clinicians and scheduling staff agree on the assessment criteria but still arrive at different priorities for the same requirement, this is a requirements conflict that should be resolved like any other.
Defining the stakeholders to be involved is one of the recommended steps for performing prioritization.

questions.explanation: (1) Ad hoc techniques such as MoSCoW rely on expert judgment based on a single, subjective criterion. (2) The syllabus notes that prioritization is often based on multiple assessment criteria such as business value, urgency, effort, and dependencies, so insisting on a single fixed criterion is false. (3) Diverging priorities despite agreed criteria are explicitly treated as a requirements conflict to be resolved like any other. (4) Defining the stakeholders to be involved is explicitly listed as one of the steps for prioritization.

questions.prompt:
HomeGrid's team discusses the three life-span categories of work products described in the syllabus: temporary, evolving, and durable.

Which of the following statements about these life-span categories is **NOT** correct?

options.text: Temporary work products are created to support communication and shared understanding in the moment, and are typically discarded afterward
Evolving work products typically emerge over several iterations and need some metadata to be managed over time
Durable work products have been baselined or released and need a full set of metadata
A temporary work product can never become a durable work product directly — it must first pass through the evolving category

questions.explanation: Per the syllabus, a temporary work product can become evolving (by keeping it and adding metadata) **or** become durable directly, by being baselined or released — it does not have to pass through the evolving category first. Statements A, B, and C correctly restate the definitions of temporary, evolving, and durable work products.
questions.reference: EU3.1.1 — Characteristics of Work Products (Life Span)

questions.prompt:
The Requirements Engineer is defining the system boundary for the HomeGrid hub. The hub exchanges data with the solar inverter, the battery management unit, GridWest Energy's demand-response signal feed, and the homeowner's mobile app. Weather-forecast data arrives only indirectly, via a third-party cloud API that the app's own cloud backend queries.

Which statement correctly applies the concepts of system boundary and context?

options.text: GridWest Energy's demand-response feed lies outside the context boundary, because utility companies are not RE stakeholders
The system boundary separates HomeGrid from its context, while RE-relevant context elements (such as the inverter and the app) lie between the system boundary and the context boundary
The solar inverter and battery management unit lie within the system boundary, because HomeGrid directly controls them
System boundary and context boundary mean the same thing and can be used interchangeably
The weather-forecast API lies within the system boundary, since its data indirectly influences HomeGrid's scheduling decisions

questions.explanation: The syllabus defines the system boundary as separating the system from its context, and the (system) context as the area between the system boundary and the context boundary where RE-relevant elements (such as the inverter, battery unit, and app) reside. The inverter/battery are context elements interacting with the hub via interfaces, not internal components; GridWest is a legitimate stakeholder, so C is wrong; and system boundary and context boundary are distinct concepts, so E is wrong.

questions.prompt: Which classification best fits the following HomeGrid requirement candidate: "The HomeGrid hub shall only communicate with certified Zigbee 3.0 devices, since BrightVolt Installers' existing inventory and the national electrical-safety approval are limited to that protocol"?

options.text: Domain requirement, because it concerns the application domain only
Quality requirement, because it concerns the reliability of communication
Functional requirement, because it describes a system function
Constraint, because it limits the solution space, for reasons beyond what is needed to meet functional or quality requirements

questions.explanation: Constraints limit the solution space for reasons beyond functional or quality needs — here, existing installer inventory and regulatory approval, not a behavior (functional) or a quality attribute (performance, reliability, etc.).
questions.reference: EU1.1 — Requirements Engineering: What (Kinds of Requirements)

questions.prompt:
A HomeGrid system requirements specification contains the sentence: "The app shall handle all abnormal sensor readings appropriately."

Which pitfall of technical writing does this sentence most clearly exhibit?

options.text: Passive voice, which should be used with care
Nominalization, turning a verb into a noun
Incomplete description, since the sentence never defines what counts as an "abnormal" reading or what "appropriately" means in practice
Incomplete comparison, which should be avoided
Universal quantifier ("all"), which should be used with care

questions.explanation: "Incomplete descriptions" is explicitly listed among the pitfalls to avoid; "abnormal" and "appropriately" leave the actual required behavior fully unspecified. Option E is a plausible near-miss since "all" is a universal quantifier to be used with care, but that alone does not make the sentence unusable — the deeper defect is the missing description.

questions.prompt:
Before submitting the HomeGrid firmware v2.3 release package to the national electrical-safety authority for certification, the device-firmware team freezes a specific, consistent set of work products: the validated system requirements specification v4.1, the approved interface description v2.0, and the signed-off test plan v1.3. No further changes to this set are permitted until certification completes.

Which of the following statements about this situation, and about requirements configurations and baselines in general, is **NOT** correct?

options.text: Every configuration that has ever existed automatically becomes a baseline the moment a new version of any work product it contains is produced
A requirements configuration contains at most one version of each work product it is defined over
A baseline is a stable, change-controlled configuration of work products used for release planning or other delivery milestones — exactly what the firmware team has created here
Configurations are characterized by properties such as logical connection, consistency, uniqueness, unchangeability, and providing a basis for reset

questions.explanation: A configuration only becomes, or serves as, a baseline when it is deliberately frozen as a stable, change-controlled set for a specific delivery milestone — producing a new work-product version elsewhere does not automatically or retroactively turn any configuration into a baseline. Statements B, C, and D correctly restate the syllabus's definitions and properties of configurations and baselines, and C correctly identifies the firmware team's certification freeze as a baseline.

questions.prompt:
When HomeGrid first launched, its ability to automatically reconnect to Wi-Fi after a router reboot delighted early customers. Three years and several competitor products later, homeowners now simply expect this behavior and would leave scathing reviews if a firmware update ever broke it — even though almost nobody explicitly asks for it anymore.

According to the Kano model, what has this requirement become today?

options.text: A delighter, since it was originally introduced as an exciting new feature
An indifferent requirement, since customers no longer care about it either way
A satisfier, since customers consciously request it in surveys
A dissatisfier, since it is now taken for granted, and its absence causes dissatisfaction even though its presence goes largely unnoticed

questions.explanation: The Kano model shows requirements migrating from delighter to satisfier to dissatisfier over time as a market matures; once a feature is taken for granted and its absence (not its presence) causes strong reactions, it has become a dissatisfier. Option C is wrong because satisfiers are consciously and explicitly requested, which the scenario explicitly rules out.

questions.prompt: Name the TWO requirements below that are correctly formulated using the EARS **event-driven** phrase template ("WHEN \<trigger> the \<system> shall \<response>").

options.text: "IF the solar inverter reports a ground-fault signal, THEN the HomeGrid hub shall disconnect the battery within 500 ms."
"WHILE the house is in 'Away' mode, the HomeGrid hub shall disable manual thermostat overrides from wall panels."
"The HomeGrid hub shall log all battery state-of-charge readings every 60 seconds."
"WHEN the battery state-of-charge drops below 10%, the HomeGrid hub shall send a low-battery alert to the mobile app."
"WHEN the homeowner's utility account is upgraded to a time-of-use tariff, the HomeGrid hub shall re-optimize the appliance schedule for the new tariff."
"WHERE the optional solar-export feature is installed, the HomeGrid hub shall report exported kWh to GridWest Energy daily."

questions.explanation: The event-driven template ("WHEN \<trigger> the \<system> shall \<response>") fits D and E, both triggered by a discrete external event. A uses the unwanted-behavior template ("IF...THEN"), B is state-driven ("WHILE"), C is ubiquitous, and F is an optional feature ("WHERE").
questions.reference: EU3.3 — Template-Based Work Products (EARS Phrase Templates)

questions.prompt:
The BrightVolt installer team and the HomeGrid firmware team both assumed, without ever writing it down, that "the hub" always refers to the physical in-home gateway device, not the mobile app. When a new firmware engineer joined and used "hub" to mean the cloud backend service instead, confusing design discussions followed for weeks before anyone noticed the mismatch.

Which RE principle was violated, and which practice could have prevented it?

options.text: Validation; the team should have run a beta test with homeowners
Shared understanding; a project glossary with an agreed definition of "hub" could have prevented the mismatch
Innovation; the team missed an opportunity to rename the hub
Evolution; the team should have accepted that terminology naturally changes over time

questions.explanation: This is a classic shared-understanding/terminology mismatch (Principle 3); the syllabus explicitly recommends glossaries as a proven practice for achieving shared understanding of terms. It is not a validation issue (checking stakeholder agreement on requirements content, not term definitions), nor evolution or innovation.

questions.prompt: BrightVolt and the HomeGrid product team are eliciting requirements for a next-generation hub. Name the TWO activities below that count as **artifact-based** gathering techniques (as opposed to questioning, collaboration, or observation techniques).

options.text: Interviewing long-time BrightVolt installers about recurring customer complaints
Shadowing an installer during a full rooftop solar installation without interrupting their work
Mining the decommissioned first-generation hub's firmware changelogs and support-ticket logs for recurring issues
Running a two-day requirements workshop with homeowners, installers, and the utility
Analyzing one-star app-store reviews and support-center transcripts for the HomeGrid mobile app
Distributing a satisfaction questionnaire to 500 HomeGrid homeowners

questions.explanation: Mining old changelogs/support logs (system archaeology) and analyzing app-store reviews/transcripts (feedback analysis) are both artifact-based techniques that use work products, not stakeholders, as the direct source. A and F are questioning techniques (interview, questionnaire); C is a collaboration technique (workshop); E is an observation technique (field observation).

questions.prompt:
The Requirements Engineer wants a model that sketches the HomeGrid hub together with the actors in its context (homeowner, installer app, GridWest Energy's demand-response feed) and the information exchanged across each interface, without yet detailing internal data structures or behavior.

Which model type best fits this purpose?

options.text: A goal model, because it expresses stakeholder objectives
A state machine, because it shows the hub's internal states
A class model, because it best expresses the hub's external interfaces
A context model, because it specifies the structural embedding of the system in its environment and the interfaces with context actors

questions.explanation: A context model specifies the structural embedding of a system in its environment and the interfaces/interactions with context actors — exactly what is needed here. A class model focuses on structure and data, a state machine on state-dependent behavior, and a goal model on goals rather than context interfaces.

questions.prompt:
GridWest Energy commissions Solara Systems to build a bespoke demand-response gateway add-on exclusively for GridWest's own grid-balancing program, under a fixed-price contract. GridWest's engineers already know precisely what the gateway must do and want a complete requirements specification signed off before development starts, to serve as the contractual basis. Requirements are expected to rarely change afterward.

Which of the following statements about this situation and about RE process configurations in general is **NOT** correct?

options.text: The Participatory RE process is iterative, exploratory, and customer-specific, with stakeholders strongly involved in both RE and development — unlike the arrangement described here
The Product-Oriented RE process is iterative, explorative, and market-oriented, typically used when an organization develops software to sell as a product or service
The syllabus's named RE process configurations are exhaustive — every real system and development context must conform exactly to one of them
GridWest's situation — a signed-off specification as contractual basis, with little stakeholder interaction afterward — is the textbook application case for a Contractual RE process

questions.explanation: The syllabus explicitly notes that these named configurations do not cover every situation — for example, regulatory constraints may impose a process that conforms to a given standard instead, so treating the three configurations as exhaustive is incorrect. Statements A, B, and D correctly restate each configuration's defining facets and application case, and D correctly identifies GridWest's fixed-price, specification-as-contract scenario as the Contractual RE process's textbook case.
questions.reference: EU5.3 — Configuring a Requirements Engineering Process

questions.prompt:
In the HomeGrid stakeholder list, GridWest Energy is documented as the party that defines mandatory demand-response signal formats the hub must support, and that can legally require curtailment of non-essential appliance loads during grid emergencies.

Which stakeholder role best characterizes GridWest Energy here?

options.text: Developer, because it defines technical signal formats
Authority, because it imposes mandatory rules the system must comply with
Sponsor, because it funds HomeGrid's development
User, because it interacts with the appliance-scheduling feature

questions.explanation: GridWest imposes mandatory rules (signal formats, legal curtailment powers) the system must comply with, which is the defining trait of an authority stakeholder role, distinct from user, sponsor, or developer roles.

questions.prompt:
A simplified HomeGrid UML class diagram shows a "Household" class associated with a "Device" class. The association end next to "Device" is labelled "0..*" and the end next to "Household" is labelled "1".

Which statement correctly interprets this relationship?

options.text: Each Household belongs to exactly one Device
A Device must belong to at least one Household and at most one Household at the same time, regardless of the multiplicities shown
Each Device belongs to exactly one Household, while a Household may be associated with any number of Devices, including zero
The multiplicities describe behavior over time (state transitions), not a structural relationship

questions.explanation: A multiplicity of "1" at the Household end and "0..*" at the Device end means each Device is linked to exactly one Household, while a Household can have any number of Devices, including none — this is a structural relationship between classes, not a behavioral/state concept.

questions.prompt:
BrightVolt's regional sales director writes: "Homeowners in colder climates need the hub to pre-heat their home before they wake up, to reduce morning energy-price spikes." This is captured purely as a description of what homeowners want from their own perspective, before any system design work begins.

Which kind of requirement is this primarily?

options.text: User requirement, because it expresses what users (homeowners) want from their own perspective
System requirement, because it specifies what the hub shall do
Domain requirement, because it concerns properties of the energy market domain
Business requirement, because it concerns Solara Systems' business goals

questions.explanation: The statement expresses what homeowners (users) want from their own perspective, before system design — the definition of a user requirement, distinct from system requirements (what the system shall do) or business requirements (organizational goals).
questions.reference: EU1.3 — Requirements Engineering: Where (Kinds of Requirement Occurrence)

questions.prompt: For each short HomeGrid scenario below, decide whether the stated conflict type is correctly identified.

statements.text: The German market team and the Canadian market team disagree on the mandatory maximum circuit-breaker trip threshold, because each country's electrical code genuinely requires a different value. This is classified as a **subject matter conflict**.

The installer team insists GridWest's demand-response signal arrives "within 2 seconds," based on an old test report, while the firmware team insists it is "within 10 seconds," based on a newer log file; each believes their own source is correct. This is classified as a **data conflict**.

Two senior architects have clashed repeatedly on past projects and now reflexively oppose each other's technical proposals in every HomeGrid design review, regardless of the proposal's merits. This is classified as a **structural conflict**.

The firmware team wants the battery-control algorithm centralized on the hub, while the app team wants parts of it to run in the cloud for faster updates, because the firmware team reports to a different VP with limited headcount who resists ceding control. This is classified as a **structural conflict**.

questions.explanation: (1) Different, genuinely factual needs caused by different legislation is the textbook subject matter conflict. (2) Parties relying on inconsistent data sources and each believing their own is correct is a data conflict. (3) Statement 3 describes a relationship conflict (negative past experience driving reflexive opposition), not a structural conflict, so the classification given is false. (4) Inequality of power/resources (limited headcount, resistance to ceding control) is the hallmark of a structural conflict.
questions.reference: EU4.3 — Resolving Conflicts regarding Requirements (Conflict Types)

questions.prompt:
Consider this HomeGrid requirement candidate: "The system shall make appliance scheduling fast and user-friendly, except in cases where the installer thinks otherwise."

Name the TWO quality criteria for single requirements that this requirement violates most clearly.
questions.explanation: "Fast" and "user-friendly" are vague, undefined terms (violating Unambiguous), and there is no measurable threshold to test pass/fail against (violating Verifiable). The requirement may still be Necessary and arguably Adequate in intent; its core problem is vagueness and untestability, not missing content (Complete) or Understandable wording as such.
questions.reference: EU3.8 — Quality Criteria for Single Requirements

questions.prompt: Name the THREE prioritization techniques below that the syllabus classifies as **ad hoc** prioritization techniques (as opposed to analytical techniques).

options.text: Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) pairwise comparison of all requirements
A weighted scoring model combining benefit, cost, and risk criteria with stakeholder-assigned weights
A multi-criteria weighted sum including benefit, cost, and time-to-implement, calculated by the product team
Kano-analysis-based classification used loosely to sort requirements into must-/should-/could-haves
MoSCoW prioritization (Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have this time)
Top-10 ranking performed by a small group of experienced installers

questions.explanation: The handbook names Top-10 ranking, MoSCoW, and loosely-applied Kano-based sorting as common ad hoc techniques, based on expert judgment along a single (subjective) criterion. Weighted scoring models and AHP (B, D, F) are analytical techniques, assigning weights to multiple criteria and calculating priorities systematically.

questions.prompt:
The Requirements Engineer needs to specify how the HomeGrid hub decides whether to charge the battery, discharge it, or export solar power to the grid — including the sequence of checks (battery state of charge, time-of-use tariff, weather forecast) and which component is responsible for each check.

Which of the following statements about model types for this kind of problem is **NOT** correct?

options.text: A UML activity diagram is well suited here, since it specifies the sequence of actions, the control flow between them, and who is responsible for each action
A context diagram is the right choice to model this decision sequence, since it depicts the internal step-by-step logic of a system's decision-making
A UML class diagram (a structure/data model) describes the static structure of a system — its entities, attributes, and relationships — rather than a decision sequence
A UML state machine diagram models event-triggered transitions between discrete states, which is a narrower fit here than a model built around actions and responsibilities

questions.explanation: Context diagrams model a system together with its external actors and environment (EU3.4.2) — they do not depict a system's internal step-by-step decision logic, which is instead the role of function/flow models such as activity diagrams. Statements A, C, and D correctly describe activity, class (structure/data), and state-machine models respectively.

questions.prompt:
During a HomeGrid requirements walkthrough, as soon as a reviewer points out that a requirement is ambiguous, the author immediately starts proposing rewording options, and the group spends the rest of the session debating phrasing for that single requirement, never getting through the rest of the document.

Which important aspect of requirements validation was violated here?

options.text: Separating the identification and the correction of defects

questions.explanation: Fixing the wording immediately instead of first cataloguing all defects, then correcting them afterward, violates the principle of separating defect identification from defect correction during validation, which is needed to keep reviews efficient and complete.

questions.prompt:
An installer suggests HomeGrid should add a "vacation mode" button, inspired by a competitor's product, before anyone has asked homeowners whether they actually have this problem or clarified what the resulting requirement should be.

Which principle explains why the Requirements Engineer should still work to separate the problem, the requirement, and the solution idea from each other, even though the solution idea came first?

options.text: Principle 2 (Stakeholders): only installers' needs matter for prioritizing features
Principle 6 (Validation): the feature should go straight into the deployed system
Principle 8 (Innovation): new features should always be implemented directly without analysis
Principle 5 (Problem–Requirement–Solution): although intertwined and able to emerge in any order, they should be thought about, communicated, and documented separately wherever possible

questions.explanation: Principle 5 acknowledges that solutions can precede requirements (as with innovation), but Requirements Engineers should still separate problem, requirement, and solution as far as possible when thinking, communicating, and documenting, to keep RE tasks manageable.

questions.prompt:
The HomeGrid thermostat's statechart shows states "Idle," "Heating," and "Defrost," with a transition from "Heating" to "Defrost" triggered by the event "outdoor-coil ice sensor = true," and a transition back to "Heating" triggered by "defrost cycle complete." While in "Defrost," the heating element is switched off.

What does this model best express?

options.text: Events that trigger transitions between states, and the actions performed during those states
The static structure and attributes of the thermostat's components
The business process for scheduling a thermostat installation
The context and external actors interacting with the thermostat

questions.explanation: State machines model events that trigger transitions between states and the actions performed during states/transitions — exactly what the ice-sensor-triggered Defrost transition and associated heating-element action describe. This is not a structural model (A), a process model of a business activity (C), or a context model (D).

questions.prompt:
The homeowner wants the HomeGrid app to always prioritize cost savings when scheduling appliances, while the installer (acting on GridWest's behalf) wants it to always prioritize grid stability during peak-demand events. Both sides insist their own priority is fundamentally "the right thing to do" for the energy transition, and neither will budge even after lengthy discussion — a value conflict.

Name the TWO conflict-resolution outcomes that are most realistic in this situation.

options.text: Overruling by a randomly chosen junior team member to save time
Definition of variants — e.g., offering both a "cost-saving" mode and a "grid-stability" mode as selectable options
A public vote among a large, anonymous user base
A full agreement where both parties completely adopt the same preferred option
Looking for higher values that unite the parties, aiming at mutual understanding and recognition of each other's principles, even if a full resolution isn't achievable

questions.explanation: The handbook states that value conflicts are notoriously difficult to resolve, with the best achievable outcome often being mutual understanding/recognition of each other's principles by looking for unifying higher values; definition of variants (offering separate configurable options) is explicitly named as suitable for value conflicts. A full agreement is unlikely given the described entrenchment, and voting/overruling are poor fits for value conflicts.
questions.reference: EU4.3 — Resolving Conflicts regarding Requirements (Resolution Techniques)

questions.prompt: Decide whether each statement about HomeGrid work-product documentation practice is True or False.

statements.text: Because the system requirements specification already states "response time must be fast" in the quality chapter, the use case for appliance scheduling may repeat the same statement in its own words to be safe.
If the HomeGrid glossary defines "Hub" and "Gateway" as synonyms, both terms may continue to be used interchangeably throughout all requirements documents without ever being marked as synonyms.

A system requirements specification that documents both high-level business goals and very detailed firmware-timing requirements in the same unstructured list, without separating abstraction levels, makes the document harder to use.
Deciding which work products will be used (e.g., use cases vs. user stories) is best left ad hoc, as each new requirement is elicited, rather than agreed upon early in the project.

questions.explanation: (1) Redundant restatement should be avoided by referencing content instead of repeating it. (2) Synonyms must be explicitly marked as such in the glossary, not just used interchangeably. (3) Mixing abstraction levels without structure does make a large document harder to use, as the syllabus recommends separating them. (4) Planning which work products to use should happen early, not ad hoc as each requirement emerges.

questions.prompt:
GridWest Energy's grid engineers are available for only two workshops at the very start of the HomeGrid demand-response gateway project, and explicitly state they cannot support any further meetings until final acceptance testing, many months later.

Which of the following is **NOT** one of the factors the syllabus identifies as influencing the configuration of an RE process?

options.text: Capability and availability of stakeholders — the factor that GridWest's limited availability most directly constrains
Experience of the Requirements Engineers involved
The programming language chosen to implement the system

questions.explanation: The syllabus's nine influencing factors cover process fit, development context, stakeholder capability/availability, shared understanding, complexity/criticality, constraints, time/budget, requirements volatility, and RE-team experience — the implementation programming language is not among them. Statement A correctly identifies why GridWest's limited stakeholder availability (only at the start, none until acceptance testing) constrains the process choice; B and C are also genuine, correctly-named influencing factors.

questions.prompt:
Before the HomeGrid battery-safety firmware (which disconnects the battery during a detected ground fault) can be released, national safety regulations require a documented, audit-trailed review performed by an independent moderator, with peer and domain experts checking the requirements against applicable electrical-safety standards.

Which validation technique best fits this situation?

options.text: A/B testing two versions of the requirement in production
Alpha testing with a small group of friendly homeowners
An informal walkthrough led by the requirement's author
A formal inspection, led by an independent moderator, following a documented process and producing an audit trail

questions.explanation: The need for an independent moderator, a documented/audited process, and compliance checking against standards is the defining profile of a formal inspection, as opposed to the more informal, author-led walkthrough or exploratory techniques like alpha/A-B testing.

questions.prompt:
Two HomeGrid teams have started separately maintaining their own private lists of term definitions for "demand-response event," each slightly different, inside their own team wikis.

Which glossary rule is being violated here?

options.text: Make the use of the glossary mandatory
Manage the glossary centrally, with a single definitive source, rather than multiple disconnected copies
Use a uniform style and structure for the glossary
Check work products for proper glossary usage

questions.explanation: Maintaining separate, inconsistent copies of definitions directly violates the rule to manage the glossary centrally, with one authoritative source rather than fragmented team-level lists.

questions.prompt: Decide True or False for each statement about traceability in the HomeGrid project.

statements.text: Linking the firmware requirement "disconnect battery within 500 ms of ground fault" forward to its corresponding automated test case is an example of explicit traceability.

If the HomeGrid specification consistently structures every requirement using the same numbering scheme and section hierarchy, without any explicit links, this can still provide a form of implicit traceability.

Traceability only needs to capture the forward relationship from a requirement to a test case; tracing a requirement backward to the stakeholder or document that originated it is not part of traceability.
A traceability matrix is one possible representation form for documenting explicit traceability.

questions.explanation: (1) Linking via unique identifiers to a test case is explicit traceability. (2) Consistent structuring/standardizing of work products is precisely how implicit traceability is achieved. (3) Traceability includes both backward tracing to origin (stakeholders, documents) and forward tracing to successors, so statement 3 is false. (4) Matrices are explicitly named as a common representation form for explicit traceability.

questions.prompt:
Solara Systems is building the next HomeGrid app release using short two-week iterations, with the product owner continuously re-ranking upcoming features as market feedback arrives, while the team visualizes the whole release's user journey from "installation" to "ongoing optimization."

Name the TWO documentation structures best suited to this way of working.

options.text: A vision document, intended to precede a linear specification phase
A business requirements specification, focused solely on Solara's internal business goals
A product backlog, which the product owner can continuously re-prioritize
A story map, to visualize the user journey and organize backlog items along it
A classic system requirements specification document, fully detailed and signed off before coding starts

questions.explanation: Continuous re-prioritization fits a product backlog, and visualizing the user journey end-to-end fits a story map — both are the alternative documentation structures named for iterative, feedback-driven work, unlike a linear, fully detailed specification, business requirements specification, or vision document.
questions.reference: EU3.6 — Requirements Documents and Documentation Structures

questions.prompt: Decide whether each HomeGrid elicitation activity below is correctly classified as True (a design/idea-generating technique) or False (it is actually a gathering technique, not a design/idea-generating one).

statements.text: A cross-functional brainstorming session where firmware, app, and product-design staff sketch "what if the hub could predict blackouts" ideas, with no stakeholder present.
Interviewing individual homeowners about their current frustrations with manual thermostat scheduling.
Building a rough interactive mock-up of a redesigned "vacation mode" screen to explore new interaction ideas with the design team, independent of any specific stakeholder request.
Reviewing the legacy hub's old support tickets to extract recurring complaints.

questions.explanation: (1) Open-ended brainstorming without stakeholders is a creativity/idea-generating technique. (2) Interviewing stakeholders is a questioning (gathering) technique, not idea-generating. (3) Building a mock-up to explore new ideas independent of stakeholder requests is prototyping used as a design/idea-generating technique. (4) Reviewing old support tickets is an artifact-based gathering technique (system archaeology/feedback analysis), not idea-generating.
questions.reference: EU4.2 — Elicitation of Requirements (Design and Idea-Generating Techniques)

questions.prompt: Decide True or False for each statement about the role of a Requirements Engineer and the value of RE, as applied at Solara Systems.

statements.text: "Requirements Engineer" is typically a distinct job title rather than a role that people with various job titles (e.g., product owner, business analyst) can play.
Adequate RE reduces the risk of building the wrong HomeGrid feature set and provides a basis for estimating development effort.
Rushing straight into firmware coding without clarifying requirements, and assuming requirements are self-evident, are both typical causes of inadequate RE.
Because the HomeGrid product owner already has deep domain knowledge, no dedicated RE skills or education are needed on the team.

questions.explanation: (1) Requirements Engineer is typically a role, not a distinct job title — business analysts, product owners, and developers can all act in this role. (2) This directly restates the stated value of adequate RE. (3) Rushing into building and assuming self-evidence are explicitly listed causes of inadequate RE. (4) Inadequate RE education/skills is listed as a cause of poor RE regardless of domain knowledge elsewhere on the team.
questions.reference: EU1.2/EU1.5 — Why RE & the Role of a Requirements Engineer

questions.prompt:
To validate the layout of the new "energy flow" screen with homeowners before any real functionality is built, the HomeGrid UX team creates clickable screens using real screen designs and real click-flows — but tapping any button only moves to the next static screen; nothing is actually computed or connected to live data.

Which kind of prototype is this?

options.text: Native prototype, a high-fidelity implementation of critical parts of the system
Evolutionary prototype, forming the core of the final system
Mock-up, a medium-fidelity prototype with real screens and click-flows but no real functionality

questions.explanation: Real screens and click-flows without real functionality is the definition of a mock-up (medium-fidelity exploratory prototype), as opposed to a low-fidelity wireframe sketch or a high-fidelity native prototype with working functionality.

questions.prompt:
Solara Systems releases a new HomeGrid firmware version every two weeks and runs a short beta-feedback survey with 50 volunteer homeowners after each release, explicitly expecting that some requirements will be added, removed, or reworded based on what they learn.

Name the TWO RE principles that this way of working most directly reflects.

options.text: Principle 6 — Validation (short feedback loops check whether desires and needs are actually met)
Principle 7 — Evolution (expecting and planning for requirements to change is the normal case, not an accident)

questions.explanation: Short feedback loops after each release directly implement ongoing validation (checking whether desires/needs are met), and deliberately planning for added/removed/reworded requirements over time directly reflects the Evolution principle that changing requirements are the normal case, not an accident.

questions.prompt:
While eliciting requirements for the new demand-response gateway, the Requirements Engineer discovers that a national regulation mandates a maximum 4-second response time for any command that curtails residential load during a grid emergency.

Which category of requirements source does this regulation represent?

options.text: A domain requirement, which is a kind of requirement rather than a source
A system, since regulations often originate from legacy systems
A stakeholder, since the regulator is a kind of stakeholder
An additional source: a legal or regulatory document

questions.explanation: Requirements sources are classified as stakeholders, documents, or systems; a regulation is a written artifact, specifically listed among additional sources as a "legal or regulatory document," distinct from the regulator as a stakeholder (authority) role.

questions.prompt:
A HomeGrid "System Requirements Specification" chapter mixes, in a single undifferentiated list, a high-level stakeholder goal ("reduce homeowners' electricity bills"), a system requirement ("the hub shall shift non-essential appliance loads to off-peak hours"), and a firmware-level detail ("the relay-switching routine shall complete within 50 ms of a scheduling decision"), all without any structure distinguishing them.

What does this illustrate, and what does the syllabus recommend?

options.text: Requirements at different abstraction levels should not be mixed; large work products should be structured so that requirements on different abstraction levels are kept separate
This is acceptable, since small and medium-sized work products are always allowed to mix abstraction levels freely
Abstraction levels only matter for model-based work products, not natural-language ones
This is purely a quality-requirements problem, not an abstraction-level problem

questions.explanation: The syllabus explicitly warns against mixing requirements on different abstraction levels in large work products and recommends structuring the specification so levels are kept separate — exactly the fix needed here.

questions.prompt:
Solara Systems is evaluating RE tools and wants one capability in particular: the ability to define custom requirement attributes (e.g., "safety-criticality"), track version history, and manage change requests for the HomeGrid specification as it evolves across releases.

Which category of RE tool support does this capability belong to?

options.text: Documentation of knowledge about the requirements

questions.explanation: Defining attributes, tracking versions/configurations, and managing changes are explicitly listed under "management of requirements" tooling, distinct from managing the RE process itself (measuring/reporting on the process, workflow management).

questions.prompt:
A HomeGrid release manager generates a report showing, for each development team (Firmware, App, Hardware), the total number of open requirements assigned to that team, without listing the requirements themselves.

Which type of view does this report represent?

options.text: Aggregating view, since it shows summaries or totals calculated from a set of requirements
A baseline, since it is used for a delivery milestone
Projective view, since it shows only some attributes
Selective view, since it selects a subset of requirements

questions.explanation: A report of totals/summaries calculated from a set of requirements (counts per team) is the definition of an aggregating view, distinct from a selective view (a subset of requirements) or a projective view (a subset of attributes).

questions.prompt:
The HomeGrid system requirements specification defines "a scheduling cycle" in its glossary as "one full pass of the appliance-scheduling algorithm," but three different chapters of the same document separately describe "a scheduling cycle" as lasting 5 minutes, 15 minutes, and "until the next tariff change" respectively, without reconciling the differences. In addition, the quality-requirements chapter and the use-case chapter each separately restate the full maximum response-time value for the demand-response feature, verbatim, in case someone reads only one of the two.

Name the TWO quality criteria for work products (covering multiple requirements) that are most clearly violated.
questions.explanation: Three contradictory definitions of "scheduling cycle" across chapters of the same document is a direct violation of Consistent; restating the same response-time value verbatim in two places instead of referencing it violates Non-redundant.
questions.reference: EU3.8 — Quality Criteria for Work Products

questions.prompt:
Before signing off the HomeGrid demand-response requirements, the Requirements Engineer deliberately invites the firmware lead, the installer lead, and a GridWest grid engineer to jointly review the same requirements set, each person explicitly checking it against their own area of expertise — technical feasibility, installation practicality, and grid-code compliance, respectively.

Which TWO of the four important aspects of requirements validation does this practice most directly reflect?

options.text: Separating the identification and the correction of defects

questions.explanation: Deliberately inviting the firmware, installer, and grid-compliance experts reflects involvement of the right stakeholders, and having each check the requirements against their own distinct area of expertise reflects validation from different views. The scenario does not describe separating identification from correction, repeated review rounds, an MVP, or A/B testing.

questions.prompt: Decide True or False for each statement about the following HomeGrid user story: "As a homeowner, I want to see my real-time solar-export earnings on the app dashboard, so that I can decide whether to run the dishwasher now or later."

statements.text: This user story follows the classic phrase template "As a \<role> I want \<requirement> so that \<benefit>."
Because Cohn's original template technically marks the benefit clause as optional, it is best practice today to omit it whenever the requirement itself seems self-explanatory.
This user story is complete as a work product on its own and needs no accompanying acceptance criteria.
A phrase template like this one is primarily useful for writing individual requirements and user stories, not for documenting whole specifications.

questions.explanation: (1) The story matches the "As a... I want... so that..." structure exactly. (2) Although Cohn's original template marked the benefit as optional, it is now standard practice to always include it, so omitting it is not recommended. (3) Every user story should be accompanied by acceptance criteria to reduce ambiguity, so it is not complete on its own. (4) Phrase templates target individual requirements/user stories specifically, while document templates serve whole specifications.

questions.prompt: Name the TWO criteria below that would justify choosing an **iterative** (rather than linear) RE process for the next HomeGrid app release.

options.text: The release must be contractually fixed as the outsourcing basis for an external development vendor
The development process for this release is plan-driven and mostly linear
The national safety regulator requires a comprehensive, formally released requirements specification very early in development
Many requirements for the new energy-trading feature are not yet known up front and are expected to emerge as homeowner feedback comes in
Homeowners participating in the beta program are available throughout development for short feedback loops

questions.explanation: Requirements not known up front and emerging over time, plus stakeholders available for short feedback loops, are exactly the criteria the syllabus lists for choosing an iterative RE process. B, D, and E describe criteria favoring a linear process instead.

questions.prompt:
The HomeGrid team wants a lightweight visual "story," using domain-specific icons, showing how an installer physically walks through a house connecting the hub, the thermostat, and the battery unit during a typical installation — mainly to build shared understanding of the installation domain rather than to specify precise system behavior.

Which further model type is this?
questions.explanation: Domain story models use domain-specific symbols to depict visual stories of how actors interact with devices and artifacts, primarily to build understanding of the application domain — exactly matching the installer walk-through description, unlike goal models, sequence diagrams, or SysML block definition diagrams.
questions.reference: EU3.4.6 — Further Model Types (Domain Story Models)

questions.prompt: Decide True or False for each statement about HomeGrid requirements versioning and configurations.

statements.text: A version number for a HomeGrid requirements document typically consists of at least two parts: the version and the increment.
Once a set of HomeGrid work products has been defined as a baseline, it may still be freely edited as long as the edits are tracked.
Version control requires, at minimum, a version number, a history of what was changed, and a concept for work product storage.
A requirements configuration may contain more than one version of the same work product at the same time, as long as both are clearly labeled.

questions.explanation: (1) Version numbers typically consist of at least a version and an increment part. (2) A baseline is change-controlled; it cannot simply be freely edited, which is precisely why it is useful for release milestones. (3) These three elements are explicitly required for version control. (4) A configuration contains at most one version of each work product, not multiple simultaneous versions.
questions.reference: EU6.3/EU6.4 — Version Control, Configurations and Baselines

questions.prompt:
Consider this HomeGrid requirement: "When the homeowner taps 'Boost' in the app, the hub shall switch the battery's state from 'Charging' to 'Discharging', and shall store the new charge-rate value in the Battery record of the household's device registry."

Name the TWO aspects, other than context, that this requirement most explicitly combines.

options.text: Functional requirement vs. quality requirement classification

questions.explanation: Storing the new charge-rate value in the Battery record of the device registry is a structure-and-data aspect, and the explicit "Charging" → "Discharging" transition is a state-and-behavior aspect. The requirement does describe one action but lacks the multi-step sequence/responsibility detail that would make function-and-flow the dominant emphasis here.
questions.reference: EU3.1.4 — Aspects to be Considered in Work Products

questions.prompt: Decide True or False for each statement about RE principles as applied at Solara Systems.

statements.text: Because homeowners' circumstances, tariffs, and devices keep changing after launch, the HomeGrid team should expect and plan for ongoing requirement changes, rather than treat each change request as an exceptional failure of the original requirements work.
Giving homeowners exactly the appliance-scheduling features they explicitly asked for is sufficient; HomeGrid has no need to pursue features that might excite or surprise them.
Once the HomeGrid system requirements specification is signed off by stakeholders, no further validation is needed, since validation is only a pre-development, one-time formality.

Because Solara Systems successfully used a fully linear, document-heavy RE process on a previous industrial-control project, it should reuse that exact same process and practice set for HomeGrid without reflecting on whether it fits the new product's context.

questions.explanation: (1) This matches the Evolution principle: changing requirements are the normal case, so plan for them rather than treating each as a failure. (2) This contradicts the Innovation principle, which says more of the same is not enough. (3) This contradicts the Validation principle, which requires validation to start during RE and continue, not stop after a single sign-off. (4) This contradicts Systematic and disciplined work, which warns against reusing past processes/practices without reflecting on fit to the new context.

questions.prompt: Decide True or False for each statement about quality criteria for RE work products, as applied at Solara Systems.

statements.text: Per the syllabus's value-oriented view of quality criteria, every HomeGrid requirement must fully satisfy all quality criteria to the same degree, regardless of how much value the requirement delivers.

Adequacy and understandability are considered the most important quality criteria for a single requirement, since without them a requirement is useless or even harmful regardless of how well it meets other criteria.
A single requirement can be perfectly unambiguous and verifiable, yet still fail to be adequate if it does not reflect the stakeholders' true, agreed needs.
"Necessary" is a quality criterion that applies only to whole work products covering multiple requirements, not to single requirements.

questions.explanation: (1) Under the value-oriented view, the degree of quality-criteria fulfillment should correspond to the value a requirement creates, not be uniformly maximal for every requirement. (2) Adequacy and understandability are explicitly named as the most important criteria for single requirements. (3) Adequate is a distinct criterion (reflecting true, agreed stakeholder needs) from Unambiguous/Verifiable, so a requirement can satisfy the latter while still failing Adequate. (4) Necessary is explicitly listed among the quality criteria for single requirements, not only for whole work products.
questions.reference: EU3.8 — Quality Criteria for Work Products and Requirements

questions.prompt:
During a sprint-planning workshop, a ParcelPath business analyst sketches a quick box-and-line diagram on a whiteboard to align the team on how carrier hand-off currently works. The diagram is intended to be erased right after the meeting and is never stored anywhere.

Which life-span category (EU 3.1.1) best matches this diagram at the moment it is created?
questions.explanation: A quick whiteboard sketch meant to be erased after the meeting supports momentary communication and shared understanding, with no metadata and no intention of keeping it — the definition of a temporary work product. It has not been kept or given metadata (which would make it evolving) nor baselined/released (durable).

questions.prompt:
ParcelPath's product owner writes the following statement for the courier mobile app: "The courier mobile app shall encrypt all customer address data at rest using AES-256."

Which of the following statements about classifying this requirement (per EU 1.1) is **NOT** correct?

options.text: A functional requirement describes a behavior or result that the system must provide
Because it mandates a specific algorithm beyond what's strictly necessary, this statement is not a requirement at all — it is pure implementation detail with no requirement status
A statement that mandates a specific technical solution beyond what's needed to satisfy the underlying need is a constraint
A quality requirement addresses a quality concern, such as performance or security, not covered by functional behavior

questions.explanation: Mandating a specific technology does not strip a statement of its requirement status — it reclassifies it as a constraint (restricting the solution space beyond what's needed to satisfy the underlying confidentiality need), not "not a requirement at all."
